title: CT and Ultrasound Diagnosis of Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm with Chronic Torsion: A Case Report with Systematic Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN) is an uncommon appendiceal tumor whose chronic torsion has not been well characterized on imaging. A 48-year-old woman with an incidentally detected right lower quadrant mass underwent serial CT and ultrasound examinations over 3.5 years. Baseline imaging in 2022 showed a thin-walled tubular cystic structure with an early whirl sign at the appendiceal base. By 2024, the wall had thickened with faint calcification while the whirl sign persisted. In 2026, the patient presented with acute right lower quadrant pain; CT demonstrated nodular wall calcification and periappendiceal fat stranding that obscured the whirl sign, while ultrasound revealed a snowstorm echotexture without detectable mural flow. Emergency laparoscopy confirmed 720-degree clockwise torsion with mid-to-distal necrosis. Pathology confirmed LAMN confined to the mucosa and muscularis propria with negative margins. This case illustrates that progressive wall thickening and calcification on serial CT, combined with ultrasound, can identify chronic torsion even when classic signs are masked by superimposed inflammation.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Digital Periapical Radiography and Cone- Beam Computed Tomography for Assessment of Intrabony Periodontal Defects
abstract: Abstract Background Assessment of intrabony periodontal defects is at the heart of diagnosis, prognosis and treatment planning. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) allows three-dimensional visualization; however, digital intraoral periapical radiography (IOPA) is still the most common modality used in clinical practice because it is generally more accessible, less expensive and associated with lower radiation. While CBCT provides a better three-dimensional characterization, previous papers have reported a similar linear measurement accuracy for these imaging modalities. Objectives To compare the accuracy and agreement of digital intraoral periapical radiography (IOPAR) with cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) in the linear and angular measurement of intrabony periodontal defects. Methods This is a comparative cross-sectional study that was performed on 36 patients with intrabony periodontal defects. Standardised digital IOPA and CBCT images for defect height, depth, width and angle measurements were taken. Agreement between modalities was assessed using paired t-tests, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland–Altman analysis. Results No statistically significant differences existed between IOPA and CBCT for any parameter (p > 0.05). There were no clinically meaningful mean differences for height (− 0.10 mm), depth (− 0.18 mm), width (0.02 mm) and angle (− 0.50°). The ICC values were good to excellent, ranging from 0.87 to 0.93. Bland–Altman analysis indicated acceptable levels of bias (most observations within the 95% limits of agreement). Conclusions The linear and angular measurements of intrabony periodontal defects obtained using digital intraoral periapical radiography were comparable to those obtained using CBCT. CBCT remains superior for three-dimensional assessment of complex defect morphology and should be used selectively when additional anatomical information is likely to influence treatment planning. These findings support digital intraoral periapical radiography as an accessible, cost-effective, and lower-radiation modality for routine periodontal assessment.

title: IT Band Syndrome Secondary to Osteogenic Cysts of the Proximal Tibia: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Chronic localized pain over the proximal tibia is most often attributed to tendinopathy, degenerative disease, stress fracture, or benign bone lesions. Osteogenic cysts of the proximal tibia are rare and are usually considered as primary lesions in the differential diagnosis of a cortical lucency. It is far less recognized that such a cyst can act as a secondary trigger for chronic friction against the overlying iliotibial (IT) band, producing IT band syndrome as a consequence of the underlying bony pathology rather than as an independent process. We report a rare case in which IT band syndrome developed secondary to an osteogenic cyst of the proximal tibia. Case presentation A 45-year-old woman presented with several months of progressively worsening pain over the anterolateral aspect of the left proximal leg, aggravated by walking, prolonged standing, and stair climbing, without preceding trauma or constitutional symptoms. Examination revealed localized tenderness over the lateral proximal tibia, with pain on terminal knee movements. Plain radiographs showed a small, well-defined mixed lesion of the proximal tibia over lateral aspect, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a well-circumscribed cortical lesion with surrounding marrow edema and reactive soft-tissue change. Surgical exploration confirmed an intraosseous osteogenic cyst measuring 2.2 × 1.5 cm, with an adjacent, secondarily thickened fibrous band arising from chronic irritation of the IT band by the underlying cyst. fluoroscopy guided assessment of the lesion confirmed cystic material with a bony, cement-like consistency, in keeping with an osteogenic cyst. Complete excision of the cystic contents and the reactive fibrous band was performed. Histopathology confirmed bony material within the lesion, together with dense fibrocollagenous tissue and fibroblastic proliferation in the adjacent band, consistent with cyst-driven IT band syndrome. The patient had complete resolution of symptoms without recurrence at follow-up. Conclusions An osteogenic cyst of the proximal tibia can be an underrecognized secondary cause of IT band syndrome through chronic frictional irritation of the overlying band. Awareness of this association supports earlier imaging-directed diagnosis, appropriate intraoperative exploration, and complete excision of both the cyst and the reactive soft-tissue changes, which together provide excellent clinical outcomes.

title: Comparing Quantitative CT Patterns in Silicosis and Welder’s Pneumoconiosis: Significant Correlations with Lung Function and Identification of a Bimodal Histogram Pattern
abstract: Abstract Background: Given its progressive nature and compensation requirements, early diagnosis and objective monitoring of pneumoconiosis are essential. This study compared quantitative computed tomography (QCT) patterns in silicosis and welder’s pneumoconiosis (WP) and assessed their correlation with lung function. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 60 patients with pneumoconiosis, comprising 30 with silicosis and 30 with WP. Two radiologists, blinded to exposure data, performed QCT analysis. QCT parameters were compared between the study groups. Spearman correlation analyses were conducted between pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and QCT parameters, and between PFTs and the International Labour Organisation (ILO) classification categories. Results: In the silicosis group, a second peak, typically clustered within the range of -200 to +200 Hounsfield units (HU), was observed. This “Secondary peak” (bimodal histogram) was significantly associated with silica exposure, higher perfusion categories, and larger opacity sizes (p = 0.001, 0.007, and <0.001, respectively). Mean lung density showed a moderate negative correlation with both forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1, rho = −0.46) and forced vital capacity (FVC, rho = −0.53), whereas no significant association was found between ILO classification and PFTs. Conclusion: We defined the secondary peak in histogram analysis, linking it to increased opacity size, profusion, and silica exposure. QCT, which better reflects lung function than the ILO classification, may represent a promising option for monitoring pneumoconiosis.

title: An Extra-gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor Masquerading as an Adrenal Mass: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background: Extra-gastrointestinal stromal tumors (EGISTs) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms arising outside the gastrointestinal tract, most often in the omentum, mesentery, or retroperitoneum. Presentation as a suprarenal mass mimicking primary adrenal pathology is exceedingly uncommon, with only isolated cases reported in the literature. We describe the clinical course, diagnostic evaluation, surgical management, and pathological findings of a retroperitoneal EGIST that was preoperatively presumed an adrenocortical carcinoma. Case Presentation: A 74-year-old woman presented with left flank pain. Computed tomography (CT) imaging demonstrated a 5.8 x 6.1 x 4.9 cm heterogeneous left suprarenal mass with central necrosis, raising concern for adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), pheochromocytoma, or metastatic disease. Comprehensive hormonal evaluation was negative. CT of the chest confirmed no metastatic disease. The patient underwent robot-assisted retroperitoneal laparoscopic left adrenalectomy with periaortic lymph node dissection. Final pathology revealed a low-grade GIST (spindle cell type, 7.5 cm, CD117+) arising from retroperitoneal soft tissue with the adrenal gland identified as a separate, uninvolved structure. Staging: pT3N0M0R1 (0/4 lymph nodes positive). The patient was discharged on postoperative day 2 without complications. Conclusion: GIST should be included in the differential of large retroperitoneal suprarenal masses. Immunohistochemistry — particularly CD117 (c-Kit) — is essential for definitive diagnosis. KIT/PDGFRA mutational analysis is mandatory to guide adjuvant tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy. Multidisciplinary oncologic review is warranted given the R1 resection and paucity of outcome data for retroperitoneal EGISTs.

title: Development and Internal Validation of Prediction Models for Early CT- Defined Moderate-to-Large Pleural Effusion After Liver Transplantation: a Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background Pleural effusion is common after liver transplantation (LT), but early moderate-to-large effusions remain difficult to predict. We developed and internally validated models for a study-specific computed tomography (CT)-defined severe postoperative pleural effusion (SPPE) endpoint. Methods We retrospectively studied LT recipients treated from June 2023 to January 2026. Patients with preoperative pleural effusion or unavailable postoperative chest imaging were excluded. SPPE was defined as a new effusion within 5 postoperative days with a maximum CT-estimated pleural-fluid depth ≥ 4 cm. The cohort was divided into a training set (n = 95) and a held-out validation set (n = 32). Four LASSO-selected predictors were used in five models. Conditional out-of-fold and 1000-replicate bootstrap validation kept predictors and hyperparameters fixed. Results Among 127 recipients, 78 (61.4%) met the SPPE definition. Retained predictors were previous abdominal surgery and immediate postoperative prognostic nutritional index (PNI), C-reactive protein, and aspartate aminotransferase measured within 1 hour after LT. Logistic regression achieved the highest held-out AUC (0.658; 95% confidence interval, 0.453–0.864). Bootstrap-corrected AUCs ranged from 0.710 to 0.761. Random forest had the highest corrected AUC (0.761) but the greatest optimism (0.079), whereas logistic regression had a corrected AUC of 0.734 and the lowest optimism (0.026). PNI was the only predictor with a nominally significant post-selection coefficient (odds ratio, 0.868; P = 0.010). Conclusions Discrimination was modest, and model ranking depended on the validation method. No algorithm was consistently superior. Prospective external validation is required before clinical use.

title: Toward Optimising Multiple Sclerosis MRI Protocols: A Comparative Study of Lesion Detection and Quantitative Image Quality Across MRI Sequences
abstract: Abstract Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis relies on MRI lesion detection, yet conventional 2D FLAIR is limited by partial volume effects. This study combines per-lesion detection between 2D and 3D FLAIR, and evaluates quantitative image quality metrics across T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and 3D FLAIR at the patient level. Methods This retrospective, comparative imaging study included 23 patients diagnosed with MS according to the 2017 McDonald criteria, who underwent brain MRI on a 1.5 T scanner between November 2025 and June 2026. Each patient underwent both 2D and 3D FLAIR within the same examination, enabling head-to-head comparison of overall lesion count. Two board-certified radiologists independently counted lesions, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were measured on T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and 3D FLAIR images. Analysis included paired-samples t-test, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, effect size (Cohen’s d) and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Results 3D FLAIR detected significantly more lesions than 2D FLAIR (1229 versus 897 overall, corresponding to a median of 56 versus 38 lesions per-patient; a 37% increase; p < 0.001), with excellent inter-rater agreement for both sequences (ICC = 0.988 and 0.993, respectively; both p < 0.001). T2-weighted imaging demonstrated the highest overall SNR (33.73 ± 12.39) and CNR (13.32 ± 7.79), followed by 3D FLAIR (SNR 19.89 ± 5.59; CNR 10.91 ± 5.62), and T1-weighted imaging (SNR 9.03 ± 4.15; CNR 6.57 ± 3.39) (all p < 0.021). Effect size analysis showed very large differences in SNR between 3D FLAIR and both T1- and T2-weighted (d = 1.48 and d = 1.54, respectively), and medium to medium-large in CNR (d = 0.66 and d = 0.52, respectively). Conclusion 3D FLAIR substantially improves overall lesion detection over conventional 2D FLAIR, while T2-weighted imaging offers superior contrast for lesion delineation. These complementary strengths support incorporating 3D FLAIR and T2-weighted imaging within a hybrid MS imaging protocol where feasible to improve lesion burden assessment.

title: Multi-Feature 3D Deep Learning for Predicting Antidepressant Treatment Response from Structural MRI
abstract: Abstract Objective Accurate prediction of treatment response in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) remains a significant challenge due to individual neuroanatomical heterogeneity and the inherent scarcity of labeled clinical data. To address these limitations, we propose MAN-MDDNet, a 3D deep learning framework designed for early and precise prognosis by leveraging multi-feature structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI). Methods MAN-MDDNet leverages 3D anatomical representations learned from large-scale medical datasets to overcome the “small-sample” bottleneck typical in neuroimaging, ensuring robust feature convergence and stability. The model is inherently brain-structure-driven and uniquely fuses four complementary features—gray matter volume/density and white matter volume/density—to capture a holistic view of structural alterations. The integration of a spatial attention mechanism (SEBlock) enables the architecture to selectively prioritize biologically relevant regions. The model was rigorously validated across two independent clinical centers (adults from Hangzhou and adolescents from Jinan). Results MAN-MDDNet significantly outperformed traditional machine learning and baseline deep learning models, achieving accuracies of 85.90%–87.18% across the two clinical centers. Notably, t-SNE revealed high structural heterogeneity in the non-remission group, indicating complex resistance mechanisms. Conclusion This study presents an interpretable deep learning framework that integrates multi-feature sMRI to predict antidepressant treatment response, which may assist in personalized management of MDD.

title: Imaging-driven early intervention for BAV-IE with atypical symptoms and severe multisystem complications: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is the most prevalent congenital cardiac malformation and confers a markedly elevated risk of infective endocarditis (IE).Severe concurrent complications, including perivalvular abscess, ruptured aortic sinus aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, and complete atrioventricular block(AVB), rarely coexist in a single patient, and afebrile atypical presentations further delay diagnosis. Cardiac computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables comprehensive preoperative anatomical mapping for complex BAV-IE, yet standardized imaging-driven management experience for this extreme disease spectrum remains scarce. Methods We report a 59-year-old afebrile male patient presenting with 4 months of exertional dyspnea. Preoperative cardiac CTA with 3D volume rendering was performed to delineate valvular, perivalvular, and aortic root lesions.A composite radical Bentall-based surgical procedure was delivered, with postoperative blood culture and 3-year serial echocardiographic follow-up. All imaging data were anonymized for publication. Results CTA confirmed congenital type 0 BAV, IE with perivalvular abscess, 18 mm coronary sinus rupture forming a 5.0×4.5 cm aortic root pseudoaneurysm, and third-degree atrioventricular block.Intraoperative debridement combined with aortic root replacement, multi-valvular repair, and temporary epicardial pacing was completed successfully.Streptococcus mitis was isolated from blood cultures.Over three years of follow-up, the mechanical valve remained functionally stable, graft flow stayed unobstructed, and all clinical symptoms completely resolved. Conclusions Cardiac CTA with 3D visualization provides definitive preoperative anatomical stratification for multi-complicated atypical BAV-IE.Early radical composite surgery guided by comprehensive imaging yields a favorable long-term prognosis, even in elderly afebrile patients with four concurrent severe cardiovascular complications.This case highlights the irreplaceable role of multimodal cardiac imaging in risk stratification and surgical planning for complex BAV-associated endocarditis.

title: Zellweger Syndrome in a Neonate: Early Clinical Presentation and Diagnostic Challenges
abstract: Abstract Background Zellweger spectrum disease includes Zellweger syndrome (ZS), a rare autosomal recessive peroxisomal biogenesis condition brought on by mutations in PEX genes. Neurological problems, craniofacial dysmorphism, hepatic failure, renal cysts, and developmental delay are among the multisystem involvement that characterise it. The condition is seldom linked to gastrointestinal abnormalities such jejunal atresia. Due to overlapping clinical characteristics with other newborn disorders, early identification is still difficult. Case presentation : A male newborn who was two months old showed signs of generalised hypotonia, lethargy, and poor eating. There were no notable prenatal or perinatal problems, and the baby was delivered at term with normal APGAR (Appearance, pulse, grimace, activity and respiration) ratings. The newborn experienced delayed meconium passage, bilious vomiting, feeding intolerance, and abdominal distension at 48 hours of life. The resection of the dilated bowel segment as well as primary jejunojejunostomy were used to treat Type IIIb jejunal atresia (apple-peel deformity), which was verified by exploratory laparotomy. Feeding and bowel function improved during the uncomplicated postoperative recovery. Further testing was necessary due to persistent hypotonia & dysmorphic facial traits, such as hypertelorism, a sunken nasal bridge, a large forehead, and low-set ears. Hepatomegaly and bilateral renal cortical cysts were seen on ultrasonography. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed caudothalamic germinolytic cysts, perisylvian polymicrogyria, and bilateral frontoparietal pachygyria. The diagnosis of Zellweger syndrome was confirmed by genetic investigation that revealed pathogenic mutations in the PEX1 gene and metabolic evaluation that revealed high blood very long-chain fatty acids. Genetic counselling and multidisciplinary supportive care were started. Conclusion This instance emphasises how crucial it is to take underlying genetic and metabolic problems into account when newborns exhibit congenital gastrointestinal abnormalities and multisystem involvement. Accurate diagnosis, supportive care, prognosis evaluation, and genetic counselling all depend on early detection and interdisciplinary assessment.

title: Intraoperative technology in skull base and vascular neurosurgery: a two-stage cross-sectional national survey
abstract: Abstract Background: Skull base and vascular neurosurgery rely on diverse intraoperative technologies. Although many are well established, contemporary data describing real-world usage patterns across operative paradigms are limited. We aimed to characterise national practice and variation in intraoperative technology use within these surgical fields. Methods: We conducted a two-stage cross-sectional survey of UK and Ireland neurosurgeons via the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS). Six SBNS MedTech Committee members compiled a predefined technology list. Respondents then reported frequency of use of these technologies for three exemplar procedures: transsphenoidal approaches for pituitary adenomas, retrosigmoid approaches for vestibular schwannomas, and pterional approaches for intracranial aneurysms. Use was recorded on a four-point ordinal scale and analysed descriptively. Kendall’s tau-b rank correlation explored the relationship between surgeon experience and technology use. Results: Twenty-four responses from 21 British neurosurgical units (66% of adult/mixed units) were analysed. Technology use was strongly procedure specific. Neuronavigation was common for transsphenoidal surgery but less frequent for retrosigmoid and pterional approaches. Endoscopy displaced microscopy in transsphenoidal surgery, whereas microscopy remained dominant for retrosigmoid and pterional approaches. Indocyanine green video angiography and micro-Doppler ultrasonography were widely used for aneurysm vascular visualisation. Drills were common across procedures, alongside micro-debriders (transsphenoidal) and ultrasonic aspirators (retrosigmoid). Neurophysiological monitoring was universal in vestibular schwannoma surgery and variably used for aneurysms. Newer technologies, including augmented reality, exoscopes, intraoperative MRI, and robotics, were used infrequently. Surgeon experience showed no significant association with technology use. Conclusions: Intraoperative technology use in British skull base and vascular neurosurgery is strongly shaped by operative paradigms. Established technologies cluster around recurring procedural needs: orientation, visualisation, tissue manipulation, and neurophysiological monitoring. Newer technologies remain selectively adopted, with uptake likely influenced by cost, infrastructure, training requirements, and workflow compatibility.

title: Upper Airway Morphology on Lateral Radiographs and Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation Outcome
abstract: Abstract Purpose Treatment response to hypoglossal nerve stimulation (HNS) for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains variable despite stringent selection criteria. We evaluated whether upper airway anatomy and electrode cuff position on postoperative lateral radiographs are associated with HNS treatment response. Methods Postoperative lateral radiographs were analyzed using standardized cephalometric measurements of the spatial relationships between the hyoid bone, mandible, cervical spine, and electrode cuff. The primary outcome was reduction in the apnea–hypopnea index (AHI). Secondary outcomes included associations between radiographic measurements, responder status according to the Sher criteria, and baseline characteristics. Results Fifty-three patients (23% female) with a median age of 62.4 years and median body mass index of 27.0 kg/m² were included. Median AHI decreased from 39.3 (interquartile range, IQR, 25.8–51.8) to 24.3 (IQR, 12.6–35.4) events/hour (P < .001). Among all measurements, only the angle between the hyoid bone and electrode cuff correlated with absolute AHI reduction (Spearman’s rho = 0.39, 95% CI 0.14–0.60; adjusted P = .029). Responders also exhibited a larger angle between the hyoid bone and electrode cuff, although this was not significant after adjustment for multiple testing (P = .042; adjusted P = .111). No other radiographic parameter was associated with treatment response. Conclusion HNS significantly improved objective and subjective outcomes; however, static upper airway anatomy and electrode cuff position on lateral radiographs showed limited value for predicting treatment response. These findings suggest that non-anatomical factors, including upper airway collapsibility and arousal threshold, may contribute more to HNS outcomes than static anatomy.

title: Effects of Preoperative Coenzyme Q10 Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Wound Healing Following Orthognathic Surgery: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Objective Oxidative stress influences postoperative wound healing after orthognathic surgery. Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), a mitochondrial antioxidant, may reduce oxidative stress and support tissue repair. This randomized placebo-controlled trial evaluated the effects of preoperative CoQ10 supplementation on postoperative wound healing. Materials and methods Twenty patients undergoing orthognathic surgery were randomly assigned to receive CoQ10 (300 mg/day) or placebo for 2 weeks before surgery. Serum CoQ10 and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were measured on surgery day and 1 week postoperatively. Wound healing–related markers ( FGF2 , COL1A1 , and TNF-α ) were evaluated by RT-qPCR at 4 weeks postoperatively. Jaw function was assessed by maximum mouth opening immediately after intermaxillary fixation removal and 1 month thereafter. Facial swelling was quantified using three-dimensional facial volumetric analysis immediately after surgery and at 1 and 4 weeks postoperatively. Bone regeneration was evaluated radiographically using CBCT immediately after surgery and at 6 months postoperatively. Results Serum CoQ10 levels were significantly higher in CoQ10 group on surgery day (p = 0.023). The percentage increase in MDA levels was significantly lower compared with the control group (p = 0.038). FGF2 expression was significantly upregulated at 4 weeks (p = 0.028), whereas COL1A1 and TNF-α showed no significant intergroup differences. No significant differences were observed in facial swelling, functional recovery, or relative bone density. Conclusion and Clinical relevance: Preoperative CoQ10 supplementation may modulate oxidative stress and molecular pathways involved in postoperative wound healing after orthognathic surgery. However, these molecular changes did not translate into measurable clinical improvements within the timeframe evaluated. Trial registration: Registered in Thai Clinical Trials Registry (https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/export/pdf/TCTR20260201003) under the registration number TCTR20260201003; retrospectively registered on 1 February 2026.

title: Cross-validated radiomic SuStaIn identifies prognostically and transcriptomically distinct event-ordering phenotypes in diffuse glioma
abstract: Abstract Background Current histomolecular classifications do not fully explain outcome heterogeneity within diffuse glioma, while most radiomic approaches use static prediction or clustering. We evaluated whether Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) could identify MRI-derived event-ordering phenotypes with prognostic and biological relevance. Methods This retrospective analysis included 246 patients with glioblastoma or lower-grade glioma from the public RadGLO resource. SuStaIn models with one to three subtypes were fitted to eight predefined contrast-enhanced T1-weighted radiomic features and compared by five-fold cross-validation. Survival associations were evaluated using subtype assignments, posterior probabilities, and grade and IDH subgroup analyses. Matched RNA sequencing from 194 patients was analyzed using limma-voom and gene-set enrichment analysis. Results A two-subtype model provided the lowest cross-validation information criterion. S1 showed early shape-irregularity and multiscale kurtosis abnormalities, whereas S2 showed early compactness and wavelet intensity/texture abnormalities. S2 was associated with higher mortality after adjustment for age and grade (hazard ratio 1.77, 95% confidence interval 1.23–2.54; p = 0.002). Each 0.10 increase in S2 probability was associated with 9.2% higher mortality risk (p = 0.005) and remained significant after additional IDH adjustment (p = 0.017). Subgroup estimates were directionally consistent, with no interaction by grade or IDH status. Transcriptomic analyses linked S2 to translation, ribosome biogenesis, DNA replication, and chromosome segregation, and S1 to neuronal and synaptic programs. Conclusions Radiomic SuStaIn identified two event-ordering phenotypes that provided prognostic information beyond established clinical and molecular classifications and showed distinct transcriptomic correlates. Independent validation with harmonized and longitudinal imaging is required.

title: Evidence of Early Selective Sertoli Cell Dysfunction in Varicocele: Inhibin B Reduction in Spermatic Vein
abstract: Abstract Objective: To study specific endocrine alterations in early-stage varicocele by directly comparing hormone profiles between affected internal spermatic vein blood and peripheral vein blood. Methods: 76 patients aged 18-28 years with clinical grade 2-3 unilateral varicocele and normal peripheral Inhibin B (pINHB) and testosterone levels undergoing microsurgical varicocelectomy. Direct intraoperative sampling of affected internal spermatic vein blood compared with peripheral venous blood. Comparison of hormone levels (Inhibin B, testosterone, estradiol, FSH, LH, progesterone) between affected spermatic vein (aINHB, aT, aE2) and peripheral blood (pINHB, pT, pE2). Correlation between aINHB levels and disease severity parameters (clinical grade, ultrasound grade, venous diameter). Results: We observed a significant "hormone dissociation phenomenon": aINHB level was significantly lower than pINHB (91.4 ± 71.2 pg/mL vs. 217.8 ± 127.6 pg/mL, p < 0.0001), while aT (450.0 ± 1115.0 ng/ml vs. 26.2 ± 8.0 ng/ml, p < 0.0001) and aE2 (276.0 ± 323.3 ng/L vs. 35.2 ± 15.3 ng/L, p < 0.0001) levels were markedly higher in the affected vein. aINHB level showed significant negative correlations with venous diameter (r = -0.412, p = 0.0052), ultrasound grade (r = -0.317, p = 0.0427), and clinical grade (r = -0.286, p = 0.0483). Conclusion: We report the first evidence of isolated Inhibin B deficiency in the affected spermatic vein of varicocele patients despite normal peripheral levels, supporting a model of early selective Sertoli cell dysfunction driven by venous hypertension. This challenges conventional diagnostic paradigms and suggests aINHB as a potential biomarker for early intervention.

title: Acquired Attentional Deterioration as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Child Psychiatry: A Pediatric Case of Possible Anti-GABABR Encephalitis With a Narrative Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Background: Attentional complaints are common in child psychiatry and are often initially considered within a primary attentional-disorder framework. However, acute or subacute deterioration in attention, functioning, or emotional state may warrant diagnostic reassessment, particularly when accompanied by medical or neurological red flags. Pediatric anti–gamma-aminobutyric acid-B receptor (anti-GABABR) encephalitis is extremely rare. This report describes a child initially evaluated for worsening attentional difficulties who was subsequently classified as having possible autoimmune encephalitis with serum anti-GABABR positivity, and provides a focused narrative review of reported pediatric cases. Case presentation: A 9-year-old girl had mild attentional complaints for approximately one year, with limited impact on academic functioning. During the month before admission, her inattention worsened substantially, accompanied by emotional changes and academic decline. She was admitted after an initial outpatient concern for a possible primary attentional disorder. After admission, electroencephalography (EEG) showed increased slow-wave activity, prompting reassessment of the clinical history and further neurological evaluation. A febrile episode approximately one month before admission was then identified. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)and routine cerebrospinal fluid(CSF) studies were unremarkable. Anti-GABABR antibodies were detected in serum, whereas CSF antibody testing was negative. The case was classified as possible autoimmune encephalitis with serum anti-GABABR positivity. Clinical and electroencephalographic improvement was observed after immunotherapy. A focused narrative review of 15 previously reported pediatric cases showed sparse and heterogeneous evidence, with variable psychiatric and neurological manifestations. Reported pediatric cases with isolated anti-GABABR antibodies and those with co-existing antibodies appeared to differ in clinical context, although current evidence is insufficient for prognostic stratification. Serum anti-GABABR positivity without CSF confirmation should be interpreted cautiously within the broader clinical context. Conclusions: This case illustrates that acute or subacute functional deterioration, rather than attentional symptoms alone, may warrant reassessment of an initial attentional-disorder formulation in child psychiatry. In this case, EEG slowing was a non-specific but clinically relevant clue that prompted neurological reassessment. Pediatric anti-GABABR encephalitis showed sparse and heterogeneous evidence, with variable psychiatric and neurological manifestations.

title: Ultrasound Viscoelastic Parameters of Distal Breast Tissue in Molecular Subtyping and Prognosis of Luminal Breast Cancer: A Preliminary Imaging-Transcriptomic Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate the predictive value of ultrasound viscoelastic parameters of distal breast tissue for molecular subtyping (Luminal A vs. Luminal B) and prognosis of breast cancer, and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms through transcriptomic analysis. Methods A total of 77 patients with pathologically confirmed Luminal-type breast cancer (32 Luminal A, 45 Luminal B) were prospectively enrolled from January 2023 to April 2024. All patients underwent ultrasound viscoelastic imaging to measure elasticity and viscosity parameters in the tumor (T), peritumoral (P), and distal breast tissue (N) regions. Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on T, P, and N tissue samples from three Luminal B patients. ROC curves were used to evaluate diagnostic performance, and Spearman correlation and logistic regression were applied to assess associations with prognosis. Results Viscoelastic parameters of distal breast tissue differed significantly between Luminal A and Luminal B subtypes (all P < 0.05), while T and P region parameters showed no differences. N-VMean achieved an AUC of 0.724 for predicting Luminal B subtype (specificity 91.1%) and an AUC of 0.733 for predicting poor prognosis. Transcriptomic analysis identified 10 key genes (including COL11A1 and WASF3) differentially expressed between T and P regions, enriched in ECM-receptor interaction, focal adhesion, and cell junction pathways. Conclusion Viscoelastic parameters of distal breast tissue, particularly viscosity, can effectively distinguish Luminal A from Luminal B subtypes and show promising prognostic value. The underlying mechanisms may involve ECM remodeling and cytoskeletal regulation, positioning distal tissue as a potential novel imaging biomarker for non-invasive prognostic assessment in breast cancer.

title: Impact of AI-assisted chest radiography on clinical decision-making: A temporal analysis of CT referral rates and the proportion of positive CT in cardiology outpatient setting
abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into chest radiography (CXR) interpretation to assist in the detection of pulmonary abnormalities. However, whether AI-assisted interpretation influences subsequent clinical decision-making in routine practice remains unclear. We investigated the association between the implementation of AI-assisted CXR interpretation and subsequent clinical decision-making, focusing on chest computed tomography (CT) referral and the detection of clinically relevant pulmonary abnormalities in a cardiology outpatient setting. Methods: We retrospectively identified adult patients who underwent CXR at their first visit to a cardiology outpatient department between March 2020 and February 2024. A commercially available AI system was routinely applied to CXR examinations throughout the study period. Patients were divided into two consecutive periods according to the date of CXR acquisition, and temporal trends were additionally evaluated by acquisition year. The primary outcome was referral for chest CT within 30 days after CXR, and the secondary outcome was the proportion of CT referrals resulting in positive findings. Generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) incorporating cardiologist-level random effects were used to evaluate temporal changes in CT referral and positive CT findings. Results: A total of 9279 patients were included, comprising 5320 patients in the earlier period and 3959 in the later period. The CT referral rate was significantly higher in the later period than in the earlier period. In GLMM analysis, the likelihood of CT referral increased significantly over time (odds ratio [OR], 1.846; p < 0.001). originalAbstract:
Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into chest radiography (CXR) interpretation to assist in the detection of pulmonary abnormalities. However, whether AI-assisted interpretation influences subsequent clinical decision-making in routine practice remains unclear. We investigated the association between the implementation of AI-assisted CXR interpretation and subsequent clinical decision-making, focusing on chest computed tomography (CT) referral and the detection of clinically relevant pulmonary abnormalities in a cardiology outpatient setting.

Methods:

We retrospectively identified adult patients who underwent CXR at their first visit to a cardiology outpatient department between March 2020 and February 2024. A commercially available AI system was routinely applied to CXR examinations throughout the study period. Patients were divided into two consecutive periods according to the date of CXR acquisition, and temporal trends were additionally evaluated by acquisition year. The primary outcome was referral for chest CT within 30 days after CXR, and the secondary outcome was the proportion of CT referrals resulting in positive findings. Generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) incorporating cardiologist-level random effects were used to evaluate temporal changes in CT referral and positive CT findings.

Results:

A total of 9279 patients were included, comprising 5320 patients in the earlier period and 3959 in the later period. The CT referral rate was significantly higher in the later period than in the earlier period. In GLMM analysis, the likelihood of CT referral increased significantly over time (odds ratio [OR], 1.846; p  < 0.001). Year-to-year trend analysis demonstrated significant increases in both the overall CT referral rate (OR, 1.192; p  < 0.001) and the proportion of positive CT (OR, 1.335; p  < 0.001).

Conclusions:

Our research suggests that AI may help cardiologists' interpretation of CXR by facilitating the identification of unexpected pulmonary abnormalities and enhancing proper clinical decision-making and further diagnostic evaluation with continued use.

title: Retroperitoneal Hybrid Nerve Sheath Tumor Mimicking Malignant Imaging Manifestations: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Hybrid peripheral nerve sheath tumors (hPNSTs) is an exceedingly rare benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor, featuring elements from at least two nerve sheath tumor cells. We herein report a rare case of retroperitoneal HNST manifesting malignant imaging features. Case presentation: We reported a 40-year-old female presented with unexplained abdominal pain, with no significant personal or familial medical history. Imaging workup revealed a large solid-cystic retroperitoneal mass with internal hemorrhage, calcification and cystic degeneration. The lesion showed restricted diffusion and progressive delayed enhancement on MRI, with blurred borders adjacent to major retroperitoneal vessels and the right ureter, highly suggestive of an invasive malignant tumor. The patient underwent complete surgical resection. Postoperative histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed a benign hybrid schwannoma/neurofibroma, with no lymph node metastasis identified. The patient recovered uneventfully and remained recurrence-free during follow-up. Conclusions: Retroperitoneal hPNST can exhibit atypical imaging features that closely resemble malignant neurogenic tumors. Accurate diagnosis relies on the combined analysis of radiological findings and immunohistochemical results. This case expands the known anatomical and imaging spectrum of hPNSTs, improves clinicians’ overall recognition of this rare disease.

title: Hepatic angiosarcoma misdiagnosed in a patient with occupational chemical exposure: A case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary hepatic angiosarcoma (PHA) is a rare but highly aggressive mesenchymal malignancy which is associated with occupational chemical exposures, particularly vinyl chloride, arsenic, and other industrial agents. Its preoperative diagnosis remains extremely challenging because its imaging features frequently overlap with those of benign hepatic hemangiomas, leading to potential misdiagnosis and catastrophic delays in management. Case presentation: A 65-year-old Han Chinese male with personal history of occupational exposure in a chemical plant for over 10 years presented to the emergency department with acute, persistent, severe right upper quadrant pain accompanied by nausea, pallor, and cold extremities. His blood pressure was 97/47 mmHg, and his heart rate was 103 beats/min. Three months prior, abdominal magnetic resonance imaging performed elsewhere reported a hepatic hemangioma (original records unobtainable). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a large hepatic mass with intratumoral hemorrhage and a satellite nodule in segment IV, suggestive of a ruptured malignant tumor. Given the patient’s stable hemodynamics, Adequate liver reserve, and resectable anatomy, emergency right hemihepatectomy was performed without perioperative complications. Postoperative immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of hepatic angiosarcoma, with positive staining for CD31, CD34, and FLI-1; negativity for AFP, CK7, CK19, and CEA; and a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 10%, with P53 positivity. The patient initially recovered and was discharged, but telephone follow-up confirmed that he died approximately three months after surgery. Conclusions: This case underscores that in patients with a history of occupational chemical exposure, even remote exposure, a radiologic diagnosis of hepatic hemangioma should be interpreted with great caution. The rapid transition from misdiagnosis to spontaneous rupture and subsequent death within three months despite technically successful emergency resection, illustrates the fulminant clinical course of PHA. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion, consider timely contrast-enhanced imaging and surgical intervention, and thoroughly counsel patients regarding the extremely poor prognosis, even after apparently curative surgery.

title: Ultrasound guided Glossopharyngeal and Maxillary Nerve Blocks for Perioperative Pain Control in Adenotonsillectomy in Pediatrics: Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Background: Adeno-tonsillectomy surgery in pediatrics is associated with increased postoperative pain and discomfort, so combined bilateral ultrasound-guided glossopharyngeal nerve ( UGGNB ) and ultrasound-guided maxillary nerve ( UGMNB ) in pediatric patients undergoing adenotonsillectomy surgeries to validate previous findings & to help decrease perioperative opioid consumption and respiratory complications Objective: Efficacy of combined bilateral glossopharyngeal nerve block and bilateral maxillary nerve block on perioperative management of tonsillectomy under general anesthesia provide excellent analgesic profile & significant differences in food intake postoperatively. Methods: 40 Patients was randomly allocated into two groups: Block Group: 20 patients received combined bilateral UGGNB and UGMNB. Conventional Group: 20 patients received IV paracetamol 15mg/kg. Intraoperative hemodynamics were recorded baseline and at 15 minutes intervals. Quality of analgesia was assessed using Wong-Baker FACES scale for children more than 3 years of age up to 8 years of age and VAS score for older children every 30 minutes for 1 hours after recovery from anesthesia in PACU and every 2, 4, 8, 12, and 24 hours postoperative after transferring to the ward. For postoperative pain therapy, if pain scale scores are ≥ 4, first was IV ibuprofen 7.5mg/kg immediately postoperative. Results: -Pain was assessed by VAS or FACES scores, according to patient age, postoperative after 30 min, then at 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 hours, where group B patients had significantly lower pain scores at all-time points (p≤ 0.043) except after 24 h (p=0.355). -Time to first rescue analgesia was significantly longer in Group B than in Group C (10.9±1.9 h vs. 5.1±2.4 h, p=0.001). -Time to first rescue analgesia was significantly delayed in Group B (P = 0.001). -There was no statistically significant difference in pethidine consumption between the two groups within the first 4 hours or over 24 hours (P=0.171). -Group B patients needed significantly less Paracetamol (70% vs. 100%, p=0.020), yet, with comparable dose to Group C patients (7.1±5.5 vs. 7.8±2.3 ml, p=0.608). Conclusion: Combined bilateral ultrasound-guided glossopharyngeal and maxillary nerve blocks provide superior postoperative analgesia compared to conventional multimodal analgesia with intravenous paracetamol for tonsillectomy patients. The technique resulted in significantly lower pain scores, prolonged time to first rescue analgesia, reduced supplemental analgesic consumption, shorter PACU stay, and higher parent satisfaction, all with an excellent safety profile. Trial Registration: on clinicaltrials.gov, ( NCT07379866) at 24 November 2025.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Pathology Foundation Models and Transcriptomic Integration for Glioblastoma Survival Prediction
abstract: Abstract Background Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) is a highly aggressive glioma difficult to stratify prognostically. Whole-slide histopathology images (WSIs) and RNA-seq profiles capture complementary phenotypic and molecular characteristics, yet their individual and combined value for GBM-specific survival prediction remains insufficiently characterized. Despite the promise of recent pathology foundation models to provide richer and more transferable image representations, their added prognostic value in GBM, either alone or in combination with transcriptomic data, has not yet been established. To address these gaps, this study evaluated deep survival models based on WSIs, RNA-seq data, and their integration for overall survival prediction in the TCGA-GBM cohort. WSI representations were derived by means of a general-domain ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 as a baseline, and five recent histopathology-specific foundation-model configurations. To disentangle modality effects from differences in sample size, models were evaluated in both full and size-matched cohorts. Results Under size-matched conditions, multimodal integration consistently improved performance over WSI-only modelling across all six WSI encoders, despite the use of state-of-the-art pathology foundation models. Multimodal models achieved median C-indexes of 0.614–0.698, with a significant overall effect of modality. The CONCH-v1.5-based multimodal model achieved the highest median C-index of 0.698. RNA-seq provided the strongest prognostic signal, with held-out median C-indexes of 0.629 and 0.632 under full-budget and size-matched training, respectively. WSI-only models achieved median C-indexes of 0.543– 0.587 under full-budget training and 0.512–0.549 under size-matched training. In this limited-size cohort and frozen-weight setting, WSI encoder choice did not significantly affect full-budget unimodal performance, and pathology foundation models did not systematically outperform the ResNet50 baseline. Overall, results suggest a positive but unconfirmed trend towards additional prognostic value in GBM from integrating histopathological and transcriptomic features. Conclusions In this limited-size, frozen-encoder setting, integrating WSI and RNA-seq improved performance over WSI-only modelling across all encoders. The CONCH-v1.5-based multimodal model achieved the highest overall performance, while multimodal integration showed a positive but unconfirmed trend over RNA-seq alone. Pathology foundation models did not provide a consistent prognostic advantage over the ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 baseline. Larger independent cohorts are needed to confirm the incremental value of multimodal integration.

title: Time-dependent spinal cord pathology defines a one-month window for established experimental cervical spondylotic myelopathy models in rats
abstract: Abstract Objective: The temporal pathology of cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) remains insufficiently defined. This study systematically characterized temporal neurological, histological, and ultrastructural changes in a rat model of chronic cervical spinal cord compression to define a potential pathological window of disease progression. Methods: Thirty Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly allocated to a sham-operated control group (n = 6) and four cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) groups (n = 6 per time point). Chronic cervical spinal cord compression was induced by implanting a hydrophilic polyurethane polymer sheet into the C5–C6 epidural space. CSM rats were evaluated at 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, and 2 months after compression. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed to confirm spinal cord compression and exclude intramedullary hemorrhage or edema. Neurological function was evaluated using the Basso–Beattie–Bresnahan (BBB) locomotor scale and somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings. Gray- and white-matter pathology was assessed using hematoxylin and eosin (HE) and Luxol fast blue (LFB) staining, respectively. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to characterize ultrastructural alterations in neurons, axons, myelin sheaths, mitochondria, and microvessels. Results: (1) MRI confirmed sustained dorsolateral cervical spinal cord compression without intramedullary edema or hemorrhage. BBB scores decreased markedly during the first week and stabilized at approximately 16–17 by 1 month, whereas SEP latency remained prolonged and amplitude remained reduced. (2) Histological analysis showed progressive anterior horn motor neuron loss and dorsal column myelin damage. At 1 month, motor neuron counts had decreased to 13.83 ± 0.70, the myelinated area to 86.21 ± 2.36%, and the vacuolated area had increased to 13.79 ± 2.36% (P ≤ 0.001). (3) TEM revealed progressive mitochondrial degeneration, axon–myelin disruption, and microvascular narrowing. At 1 month, mitochondrial cristae had decreased to 4.30 ± 0.16 per profile, and the microvascular lumen-to-cross-sectional area ratio had declined to 31.00 ± 1.42%. These abnormalities persisted or progressed at 2 months, demonstrating that the pathological phenotype was established by 1 month. Conclusion: Cervical cord injury progressed in a time-dependent manner, and 1 month of compression may represent a critical pathological window for the CSM model.

title: NeuroRAD-FM: A Distributionally Robust Foundation Model for Precision Neuro-Oncology
abstract: Abstract Foundation models for neuro-oncology have shown promise for non-invasive molecular characterization and prognostication, yet their clinical utility remains limited by cross-institutional distribution shift and poor performance on under-represented molecular alterations. We developed NeuroRAD-FM, combining self-supervised pretraining, Group-DRO, and a multi-backbone ensemble to learn site-invariant imaging representations. NeuroRAD-FM is pretrained on 7,414 multi-sequence brain MRI examinations aggregated from multiple institutions and evaluated on independent glioma cohorts from UCSF (n = 111), UPenn (n = 95), and an in-house cohort (n = 292). Downstream tasks included automated tumor segmentation, molecular biomarker prediction, and overall survival prediction. Compared with conventional foundation models, NeuroRAD-FM learned more site-invariant features, improved tumor segmentation across tumor types, significantly enhanced molecular marker prediction, and increased concordance indices across all institutions. These findings suggest that integrating Group-DRO with a multi-backbone foundation model enables robust, site-invariant representation learning and substantially improves molecular subtype and survival prediction across diverse neuro-oncology cohorts.

title: Quadruple hourglass-like constrictions of the radial nerve in neuralgic amyotrophy treated by focal resection and in-situ autograft reconstruction: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Hourglass-like constrictions are increasingly recognized as a structural manifestation of neuralgic amyotrophy. When several constrictions occur sequentially within a main nerve trunk, it remains uncertain whether the entire affected segment is irreversibly nonfunctional or whether the intervening nerve tissue retains a longitudinal scaffold capable of supporting regeneration. We report a rare case of quadruple hourglass-like constrictions of the main radial nerve that provides clinical evidence for preserved regenerative capacity within the intervening nerve segments. Case presentation: A previously healthy 36-year-old woman developed severe neuropathic pain followed by complete left wrist and finger drop. Preoperative electrophysiological examination demonstrated severe left radial neuropathy, active denervation, absent or markedly reduced voluntary motor unit recruitment in radial nerve-innervated muscles, absent distal radial compound muscle action potentials, and absent superficial radial sensory nerve action potential. High-resolution ultrasonography identified four sequential constrictions from the mid-upper arm radial nerve to the origin of its deep branch. Surgical exploration was performed at approximately 4 months after pain onset. Three severe proximal constrictive foci were selectively resected, whereas the intervening structurally continuous nerve segments were preserved and used as serial in-situ autologous interposition bridges. The mild distal constriction was treated with epineurial neurolysis. Follow-up showed progressive motor recovery. At approximately 3 months after surgery, electromyography showed nascent reinnervation in proximal radial nerve-innervated muscles. Late electrodiagnostic follow-up demonstrated re-emergent radial motor responses, and ultrasound showed continuity of the reconstructed nerve across the three coaptation sites. At approximately 14 months after surgery, the patient had regained near-normal wrist and finger extension, with active thumb extension exceeding 45 degrees. Conclusions: This case suggests that severe functional impairment in neuralgic amyotrophy with multiple hourglass-like constrictions may be maintained predominantly by discrete constrictive barriers causing focal mechanical interruption or conduction block, rather than by irreversible degeneration of the entire involved nerve segment. Even when the affected nerve has undergone axonal degeneration and has been diseased for several months, preserved regenerative bands within the intervening segments may allow them to function as native conduits for axonal regrowth after the focal barriers are removed.

title: Successful Management of Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis Complicating Rheumatoid Arthritis with Whole-lung Lavage and De-escalation of Anti-rheumatic Therapy: A Report of Two Cases
abstract: Abstract Background Autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (APAP) is characterized by elevated levels of autoantibodies against granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), resulting in the accumulation of surfactant proteins within the alveoli. Immunosuppressive therapy is generally considered harmful in APAP, but the clinical impact of reducing immunosuppressive therapy on concomitant connective tissue disease remains unclear. Case presentation Case 1: A 69-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in clinical remission on methotrexate, iguratimod, and salazosulfapyridine developed exertional dyspnea. Chest High-resolution computed tomography showed bilateral ground-glass opacities with a crazy-paving appearance, and APAP was diagnosed based on bronchoalveolar lavage findings and elevated serum anti-GM-CSF autoantibody levels. Whole-lung lavage (WLL) resulted in improvement, but APAP recurred one year later and required a second WLL. During APAP management, anti-rheumatic therapy was gradually tapered and discontinued, and she remained free of both APAP recurrence and RA flare for two years after the second WLL. title: Diagnostic Utility of Pentraxin-3 Compared With N-terminal-prohormone of B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (Nt-probnp) and Tumour Necrosis Factor-α (Tnf-α) in Dogs With Degenerative Mitral Valve Disease
abstract: Abstract Pentraxin-3 (PTX3) is a novel biomarker of interest in cardiovascular disease and injury. Despite this, there is limited literature on PTX3 as a veterinary biomarker. Another ubiquitous inflammatory marker, tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), has been studied extensively in dogs with DMVD, with mixed findings. The N-terminal-prohormone of B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a routinely used biomarker of canine cardiac dysfunction. This study compared the diagnostic utility of PTX3 with TNF-α and NT-proBNP in dogs with DMVD. Serum NT-proBNP, PTX3, and TNF-α were measured in 50 client-owned dogs diagnosed and staged according to the ACVIM stages A-D. Echocardiographic variables, radiographic vertebral heart score (VHS) and vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and quality of life (QoL) scores were assessed. The Kruskal-Wallis test was used to compare PTX3, TNF-α, and NT-proBNP levels between different stages of DMVD, and the Jonckheere-Terpstra test assessed whether serum biomarker concentrations showed a significant ordered trend across progressively worsening DMVD across stages. Spearman’s correlation was used to assess the associations between biomarker levels, disease stage, QoL scores, SBP, radiographic, and echocardiographic parameters. Concentration of PTX3 and TNF-α did not differ significantly across DMVD stages, while only NT-proBNP showed significant variation between stages (p = 0.02). Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test revealed a significant ordered trend in serum NT-proBNP (p < 0.01), but not PTX3 and TNF-α across DMVD stages. NT-proBNP correlated significantly with DMVD stage, QoL score, VHS, VLAS, and echocardiographic variables including LVIDdn, LA:Ao (p < 0.01), and EF%, FS% (p = 0.02). NT-proBNP remains a reliable biomarker for diagnosis, disease monitoring, and prognosis assessment in canine DMVD. Future studies employing larger longitudinal cohorts will be essential to better elucidate the role of inflammatory markers in canine heart disease.

title: Alveolar Bone Mineral Density Correlates with Lumbar Spine Bone Mineral Density During Romosozumab Therapy: A Prospective Observational Study In Osteoporosis
abstract: Abstract Early osteoporosis detection remains challenging because of the limited accessibility of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), sparking interest in the use of routine dental radiographs to assess alveolar bone mineral density (al-BMD). This prospective observational study evaluated the longitudinal changes in al-BMD during osteoporosis therapy, its association with systemic BMD and its utility as a screening and monitoring tool in female patients. al-BMD was quantified using standardized intraoral radiographs with reference phantoms, while systemic BMD and bone turnover markers were concurrently monitored. At baseline, al-BMD was significantly lower in patients with untreated osteoporosis than in both young and elderly non-osteoporotic controls. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated high diagnostic performance for al-BMD in identifying untreated osteoporosis, showing a positive correlation with the lumbar spine BMD but not with the femoral neck BMD and the total hip BMD. During sequential bone-anabolic therapy, al-BMD significantly increased over time, eventually reaching levels comparable to those of elderly non-osteoporotic controls. Also, al-BMD changes like those observed in systematic BMD. These findings suggest that al-BMD derived from dental radiographs is a clinically promising adjunct for osteoporosis screening and monitoring treatment-associated bone improvements.

title: Chemotherapy-Refractory Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Concurrent Long-Segment Intramedullary Spinal Metastases and Brain Metastases:Case Reports and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Background Intramedullary spinal metastases (ISCM) are an extremely rare complication of systemic malignant tumors affecting the central nervous system, with a very poor prognosis,Among these, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is particularly rare as a primary tumor.To date, there have been only seven documented cases of ISCM associated with esophageal cancer,In all cases, involvement was limited to a single segment of the spinal cord.This article reports the first case of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) with long-segment intramedullary metastasis in the thoracic segment during chemotherapy, complicated by concurrent brain metastases. Case Presentation A 69-year-old male patient with advanced ESCC (cT4N1M1, with liver metastases),After receiving three cycles of albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with cisplatin chemotherapy,The patient presented with acute pain in the left shoulder and right lower limb, weakness in the right lower limb (Grade IV on the Medical Research Council muscle strength scale), and decreased sensation in the abdomen.Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the spinal cord revealed extensive intramedullary lesions spanning long segments from T1 to T12,Accompanied by characteristic ring-shaped enhancement,accompanied by characteristic ring-shaped enhancement,at the same time, edema of the cervical spinal cord is visible, but there is no enhancement.A concurrent cranial MRI revealed one new annular enhancing nodule in the left frontal lobe and one in the right cerebellum.Given the widespread involvement of the central nervous system and the family’s refusal of surgery and radiation therapy, the patient died 15 days after discharge. Conclusion Even in patients in whom systemic chemotherapy appears to be effective, ISCM can still occur, possibly due to tumor cells crossing the blood-spinal cord barrier via the hematogenous route.Gadolinium-enhanced MRI and annular enhancement are key to the diagnosis.This case highlights that when acute neurological symptoms occur during cancer treatment, the threshold for ordering neuroimaging should be lowered,this allows for early detection, thereby giving some patients the opportunity to undergo palliative radiation therapy or surgery.

title: CBCT-based evaluation of inferior turbinate morphometry and uncinate process anatomy in relation to maxillary sinus mucosal thickness
abstract: Abstract Objectives: To investigate the independent associations of inferior turbinate (IT) morphometrics and uncinate process (UP) anatomical variations with maxillary sinus mucosal thickness (MSMT) on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 200 sinus sides from 100 patients were evaluated. MSMT was measured and sides were classified as mucositis-positive (≥1 mm, n = 100) or mucositis-negative (<1 mm, n = 100). IT dimensions (height, width, anteroposterior [AP] length, and volume) and UP characteristics (orientation, pneumatization, and superior attachment type) were assessed using On-Demand and ITK-SNAP software. Cluster-robust linear regression was performed to account for within-subject bilateral dependency and adjust for potential confounders. Results: In the final adjusted multivariable model, IT height and IT AP dimension were the only variables independently associated with MSMT. Lower IT height was associated with greater MSMT ( P = 0.02), whereas greater IT AP length was positively associated with MSMT ( P = 0.006). In contrast, IT width ( P = 0.76), IT volume ( P = 0.28), UP orientation ( P = 0.51), UP pneumatization ( P = 0.77), and superior attachment type ( P = 0.45) were not significantly associated with MSMT. Conclusions: Dimension-specific IT parameters, particularly height and AP length, rather than overall IT volume or UP anatomical variation, were independently associated with maxillary sinus mucosal thickness. These findings suggest that localized turbinate geometry may be more relevant to mucosal thickening than generalized turbinate enlargement or uncinate process morphology. Clinical Significance :Understanding the anatomical variations of the inferior turbinate and uncinate process on CBCT scans helps clinicians identify potential anatomical predisposing factors for maxillary sinus mucosal thickening, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning for sinonasal and rhinogenic pathologies prior to dental implant placement or sinus lift surgeries.

title: Reversible Adrenal Hyperplasia Associated with Chronic Etomidate Use: A Case Report with 3-Year Radiological Follow-Up
abstract: Abstract Background: Etomidate, a commonly used intravenous anesthetic, is known to reversibly inhibit adrenal 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1). Illicit electronic cigarettes containing etomidate have emerged in some regions, and chronic inhalation has been associated with acquired adrenal hyperplasia. However, the long-term reversibility of etomidate-induced adrenal hyperplasia after drug cessation has not been documented in the literature. Case presentation: We report a 33-year-old male patient who presented with recurrent fatigue, after approximately 10 years of 4-5 times per week etomidate-containing e-cigarette use. Laboratory evaluation revealed hypokalemia (serum K⁺ 3.37 mmol/L), normal morning cortisol (9.66 μg/dL), elevated adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) (322.00 pg/mL), and normal aldosterone-to-renin ratio. Computed tomography demonstrated bilateral adrenal thickening (9.3mm on the right, 9.5 mm on the left). Genetic testing excluded CYP11B1 and CYP21A2 mutations, supporting an acquired etiology. The patient was advised to discontinue etomidate use. At the 3-year follow-up, the patient remained abstinent. Repeat CT imaging showed largely resolution of adrenal hyperplasia, with adrenal thickness reduced to 3.9-4.3 mm bilaterally, and biochemical parameters returned to normal range. Conclusion: This case provides the first imaging evidence that etomidate-induced adrenal hyperplasia is reversible upon drug cessation, with largely radiological resolution documented at 3-year follow-up. The diagnosis of drug-induced adrenal hyperplasia can be established through a combination of exposure history, biochemical profile, and imaging findings, even in the absence of genetic testing. Early recognition is crucial to avoid unnecessary invasive investigations or genetic workup. A conservative "watch-and-wait" approach after drug withdrawal appears to be appropriate for similar cases.

title: ThyroGuard-Net: A Sensitivity-Optimised, Explainable Hybrid CNN–Transformer Framework with Evidential Uncertainty for Thyroid Nodule Classification
abstract: Abstract Thyroid cancer is a common endocrine malignancy and the most common diagnostic technique for thyroid cancer is ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration (FNA) cytology. Although many researchers have utilized machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), recent studies still rely on small single-centre datasets, poor generalisation across institutions, class imbalance, lack of explainability and – crucially – insufficient focus on sensitivity. This article highlights the typical issues that have plagued studies over the past decade and offers the recommendation of a publicly available, relatively multi-center dataset, TN3K that can help mitigate those issues. This paper proposes a hybrid EfficientNet–Swin Transformer architecture for robust and efficient training of concept-attention networks, trained with a sensitivity-weighted Focal-Tversky loss, an evidential uncertainty module for indeterminate-case triage and a concept-bottleneck explainability layer based on TI-RADS. It presents a complete mathematical formulation for all components (pre-processing, dual-branch feature extraction, cross-attention fusion, concept-bottleneck explainability, sensitivity-maximising loss design, and evidential uncertainty estimation). The model was trained on TN3K and tested without further fine tuning on the external DDTI dataset with 87.95%/91.46%/85.60% (accuracy/sensitivity/specificity) on the test set, with an evidential triage rate of 13.03–16.95%, showing the cross-institution generalisation narrowed and clinically, calibrated uncertainty over previous single-mechanism methods.

title: Oscillatory Modulation of Tumor Microenvironment pH Enhances Simulated Therapeutic Response in Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract This study presents the BioOnco System as a computational proof-of-concept framework combining histopathological image classification with a two-dimensional reaction-diffusion model of normalized proton-field dynamics. The classification component used the publicly available BACH breast histopathology dataset comprising 400 microscopy images from four diagnostic classes: benign, in situ, invasive, and normal. The final pipeline extracted 1,536-dimensional features with EfficientNet-B3, standardized the features, and applied multiclass logistic regression. On a held-out test set of 60 images (15 per class), the model achieved 85.0% accuracy, 0.852 macro-F1, and a macro one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 0.952. Independently, the reaction-diffusion module was evaluated on a 60 × 60 spatial grid under four predefined conditions: control, chemotherapy, oscillatory modulation, and combined therapy, with 30 independent replicates per condition. The final mean normalized proton concentration was 0.7423 ± 0.0002 for control, 0.4600 ± 0.0000 for chemotherapy, 0.8693 ± 0.0002 for oscillatory modulation, and 0.2676 ± 0.0000 for the combined condition. The combined condition differed significantly from chemotherapy alone (independent two-sample t-test, p < 0.0001). These findings demonstrate distinct computational responses produced by the specified model parameterizations but do not establish clinical efficacy, experimentally demonstrate therapeutic synergy, or provide patient-specific predictions. Experimental validation and parameter calibration are required.

title: Application of CT-Based Three-Dimensional Reconstruction to Guide Anatomical Resection for Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformations in Children
abstract: Abstract Purpose To describe CT-based patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction for lesion-oriented anatomical regional resection and compare the short-term outcomes of three surgical approaches for pediatric congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM). Methods We retrospectively reviewed 185 children treated between July 2023 and March 2025: segmentectomy (n=62), lobectomy (n=66), and anatomical regional resection (n=57). Noncontrast thin-slice CT data were reconstructed using Mimics to delineate the lesion, bronchi, pulmonary arteries, and pulmonary veins. Perioperative outcomes and postoperative complications were compared among the groups. Results Age and weight did not differ significantly among the groups. Operative times were 95±5.9, 80±3.7, and 92±5.7 min, while chest tube durations were 4±1.3, 2±1.1, and 2±1.4 days, respectively (both overall P<0.001). Pneumothorax, subcutaneous emphysema, pneumonia, and localized atelectasis did not differ significantly. Radiographic compensatory pulmonary hyperinflation occurred in 2, 10, and 1 children, respectively (overall P=0.009). Conclusion Patient-specific 3D reconstruction provided an anatomically explicit basis for lesion-oriented operative planning. Anatomical regional resection was feasible; however, the observed between-group differences require cautious interpretation because treatment allocation was nonrandomized. Prospective multicenter studies with adjusted analyses and standardized imaging follow-up are warranted.

title: Medial Epiphyseal–Epicondylar Alignment and Clinical Outcomes After Adding a Medial K-Wire to Lateral Two-Wire Fixation in Gartland II–III Pediatric Supracondylar Humerus Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background Closed reduction and percutaneous pinning is standard treatment for displaced pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures, but the optimal pin configuration remains debated. We compared clinical and radiographic outcomes between lateral two-pin and medial-pin–augmented (crossed) fixation, focusing on the medial epicondylar epiphyseal angle (MEEA) as a comparative outcome rarely used for this purpose. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 202 children aged 2 to 12 years with Gartland type II to III supracondylar humeral fractures treated surgically between 2016 and 2021. Group 1 (117 children) received two divergent lateral wires plus one medial wire via mini-open incision; Group 2 (85 children) received two lateral wires only. The decision to add a medial wire reflected a mix of surgeon routine and intraoperative judgment of construct stability, not a fixed protocol. Outcomes were the Flynn rating, loss of carrying angle and elbow motion, and the Baumann, humeroulnar, medial epicondylar epiphyseal, and diaphysiometaphyseal angles, measured at final follow-up against the uninjured side. title: Diagnosis of Persistent Left Superior Venacava in Children with Conotruncal Defects using Multi-slice Computed Tomography
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) complicates surgical procedures in children with conotruncal defects (CTD). Although multi-slice computed tomography (MSCT) is widely applied in preoperative CTD diagnosis, its role in detecting PLSVC and analyzing CTD–PLSVC associations has received limited attention. This study evaluated the diagnostic value of MSCT for PLSVC in children with CTD, while examining its type, incidence, and distribution. Materials and Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 264 children with surgically confirmed CTD who underwent 320-MSCT. Image quality and radiation dose were assessed, and age-related variations in CT dose parameters were analyzed. MSCT findings of PLSVC were compared with intraoperative results. Results All MSCT images were diagnostic (mean subjective score: 3.45 ± 0.5; Cohen’s κ = 0.80). The mean effective dose was 1.02 ± 0.24 mSv, with significant age-related differences in radiation parameters. MSCT showed complete concordance with surgical findings. PLSVC was detected in 32 children (12.1%), with the highest incidence in pulmonary atresia. The most frequent anatomical type was double superior vena cava without bridging vein. Conclusions Low-dose MSCT provides accurate, non-invasive visualization of PLSVC and its anatomical variants in children with CTD, supporting precise preoperative planning. Routine MSCT evaluation of CTD should include careful assessment for PLSVC, particularly in pulmonary atresia, where prevalence is highest.

title: Gut Check! Effectiveness of Emergency Room Investigations for Acute Appendicitis
abstract: Abstract Purpose Ultrasound (US) is the most used imaging modality in children with suspected appendicitis, with high sensitivity and diagnostic accuracy. Our institution utilizes a standardized US findings reporting system evaluating for appendicitis, which may obviate the need for CT scan if findings are consistent with appendicitis. In this study, we aimed to characterize the efficacy of our protocol for emergency room appendicitis workup and identify any risk factors contributing to a missed diagnosis. We hypothesize that < 10% of patients who underwent appendectomy presented within the preceding 14 days with symptoms of abdominal pain and our current investigative framework failed to identify acute appendicitis. Methods We conducted a single institution retrospective review of all pediatric patients who underwent laparoscopic appendectomy from 2020 to 2022 to determine the rates of prior presentation to the emergency department with a negative workup for acute appendicitis in the 14 days prior to formal diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Demographics and clinical characteristics were collected. Differences between groups were compared by using the Fisher’s Exact Test or Chi-Square test for categorical variables. Results A total of 1902 patients met inclusion criteria with a median age of 11.4 years (IQR 8.3, 14.4). Most patients were male (N = 1,094, 58%), white (N = 1,244, 65%), English speaking (N = 1,695, 89%) Sixty-two patients (3.3%) were seen in the emergency department for abdominal pain within 14 days prior to appendicitis diagnosis, and an additional six patients (0.3%) were seen within the prior 30 days. These patients were younger with a median age of 7.4 years (N = 4, 12.5%) (p = < 0.001) and more likely to be non-English speaking (N = 17, 27%) (p = < 0.001). Thirteen (21%) patients had an ultrasound at initial presentation, and an additional three (5%) had a CT scan. Ultrasound findings included: Category 1 (N = 2), Category 2 (N = 5), indeterminate (N = 1), free fluid (N = 1), dilated appendix (N = 1). At the time of discharge on initial presentation, these patients were diagnosed with constipation (N = 7), abdominal pain (N = 22), gastroenteritis (N = 14), and other (N = 10). Surgery was consulted on 8% (N = 5) of these cases. Missed appendicitis patients had a higher rate of perforation (45.2% vs 27.7%, p < 0.001) and longer mean length of stay (56 hrs vs 9 hrs, p < 0.001). Conclusion Patients who presented with acute appendicitis after an initial missed diagnosis are more likely to have perforation and longer inpatient LOS. While a protocolized emergency room diagnostic workup for appendicitis is effective, barriers to effective communication with patients may contribute to missed diagnosis and should be considered in clinical decision making.
