title: Extranodal Rosai Dorfman Disease: An Unusual Course Without Nodal or Systemic Involvement- Case report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Rosai–Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare benign non-Langerhans cell histiocytic disorder that typically presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Isolated extranodal disease involving the head and neck is uncommon, while recurrent multifocal disease without nodal or systemic involvement is exceptionally rare. We report a unique case of recurrent multifocal extranodal RDD confined to the sinonasal tract and eyelid. Case Report: A woman in her late 50s presented with recurrent nasal obstruction and epistaxis. Evaluation revealed a mass in the right nasal cavity, which was excised endoscopically. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of extranodal RDD. During a 3-year follow-up, she experienced sequential recurrences involving the contralateral nasal cavity, nasal septum, anterior ethmoid sinus, and left lower eyelid. Each lesion was managed successfully with complete surgical excision, and histopathology consistently confirmed recurrent RDD. Despite multifocal recurrences, there was no evidence of cervical lymphadenopathy, systemic symptoms, or radiological features of aggressive disease. The patient remained symptom-free following each surgery and did not require systemic therapy. Conclusion This case highlights an unusual presentation of recurrent multifocal extranodal RDD involving the sinonasal tract and eyelid in the absence of nodal or systemic disease. Although recurrence is uncommon, RDD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of recurrent sinonasal masses. Histopathological confirmation remains essential for diagnosis, and complete surgical excision can provide excellent long-term disease control in patients with localized recurrent extranodal disease, avoiding the need for systemic treatment.

title: Hemorrhage-Induced Bias of [18F]FDG PET Signal Interpretation in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is associated with high mortality and poor prognosis. Most patients present with unresectable PDAC, underscoring the need for reliable non-invasive imaging biomarkers. [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography or[ 18 F]FDG PET provides metabolic information but lacks specificity for viable tumor tissue, as tracer uptake can be affected by inflammatory processes, potentially confounding tumor characterization or treatment-response assessment. This study explores the impact of hemorrhage and associated inflammatory changes on [ 18 F]FDG uptake in PDAC. Methods [ 18 F]FDG PET findings were correlated with MRI and histology in orthotopic PDAC models representing quasimesenchymal (PSN1) (n = 8; 4 hemorrhagic) and classical (HPAC) (n = 9; 6 hemorrhagic) subtypes in mice, and a clinical test cohort (n = 6; 4 hemorrhagic). Results In non-hemorrhagic murine tumors, [ 18 F]FDG PET reliably identified hypometabolic necrotic regions, allowing exclusion from analysis. In contrast, necrotic regions containing multifocal hemorrhage showed significantly higher [ 18 F]FDG uptake (HPAC SUV mean 1.42 ± 0.19 vs 1.10 ± 0.10, P = 0.036, PSN1 SUV mean 1.72 ± 0.15 vs 1.20 ± 0.14, P = 0.002). In patients, tumors with hemorrhage demonstrated higher SUV max than non-hemorrhagic tumors (7.57 ± 1.4 vs 3.41 ± 0.2). Reference-tissue normalization preserved these differences. Murine tumors exhibiting hemorrhage also showed increased macrophage infiltration. Conclusions Hemorrhage and associated inflammatory changes can confound [ 18 F]FDG PET interpretation, leading to overestimation of viable tumor tissue. Incorporating complementary structural imaging with careful region-of-interest definition improves the accuracy of [ 18 F]FDG PET-based PDAC characterization and treatment response assessment.

title: Extended Reality-Based Hepatic Surgical Planning: Impact on Task Time, Anatomic Accuracy, and Cognitive Burden in Novice Surgeons
abstract: Abstract Background : Traditional liver surgery education relies on 2D imaging and cadaveric specimens, causing misjudgments in complex 3D anatomy and hemodynamics, especially among junior surgeons. Objective : To develop LiverXR-Plan, a multimodal extended reality platform integrating structural imaging and hemodynamic simulation for education and surgical planning. Design : A prospective controlled trial compared LiverXR-Plan with 2D methods. Participants: 52 medical students and 47 residents. Interventions: Preoperative planning using 2D CT or LiverXR-Plan with 3D reconstruction and CFD simulation. Outcomes: Anatomical accuracy, completion time, and NASA-TLX workload. Results : Accuracy improved from 32.69% to 100% (students) and 74.47% to 100% (residents); time reduced by 54.40% and 51.12%. Hemodynamic visualization enabled risk prediction; workload significantly decreased. Conclusions : LiverXR-Plan enhances surgical planning competency and shifts liver surgery education from experience-dependent to data-driven decision-making.

title: Clinical Characteristics, Microbiological Profile, and Antimicrobial Resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Hospitalized Patients with Bronchiectasis: A 10-Year Single- Center Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background. Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) is the most clinically significant respiratory pathogen in patients with bronchiectasis, yet data from mainland China on PA colonization, antimicrobial resistance, and its impact on hospitalization outcomes remain limited. We aimed to characterize the clinical and microbiological profile of PA among hospitalized patients with bronchiectasis over a 10-year period. Methods. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all adult patients hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of bronchiectasis at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital, a tertiary referral respiratory center in China, between January 2014 and December 2024. Clinical, radiological, laboratory, and microbiological data were extracted from the electronic hospital information system. Respiratory samples were cultured using standard microbiological methods; antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed by the clinical microbiology laboratory. Patients were classified as PA-positive or PA-negative on the basis of respiratory culture results. Comparisons between groups used the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables and the chi-square test for categorical variables. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with PA colonization. Results. Among 7787 hospital admissions from 2,503 unique patients (mean age 59.9 ± 13.4 years; 56.4% female), 942 admissions (29.2%) underwent respiratory culture. PA was the dominant pathogen, isolated in 338 of 942 cultured admissions (35.9%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (3.0%), Acinetobacter baumannii (2.4%), and Aspergillus spp. (6.2%). PA-positive admissions were younger (median 60 vs. 64 years), had longer hospitalization (12 vs. 11 days), higher white blood cell counts (7.28 vs. 6.56 × 10⁹/L), higher platelet counts, and higher PaCO2 (51 vs. 44 mmHg) than PA-negative admissions (all p < 0.05). In multivariable analysis, CT-documented bronchiectasis (adjusted OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.19–2.24) and higher WBC count (adjusted OR 1.06 per unit, 95% CI 1.02–1.10) were independently associated with PA colonization, whereas older age was protective (adjusted OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97–0.99). Among 821 PA isolates with comprehensive susceptibility testing, 20.0% were multidrug-resistant, 26.4% were carbapenem-resistant, and 25.0% were fluoroquinolone-resistant; amikacin and tobramycin retained the highest susceptibility rates (90.4% and 93.8%, respectively). CT-documented bronchiectasis was also the strongest predictor of recurrent hospitalization (adjusted OR 3.17, 95% CI 2.46–4.07). Conclusions. PA is the predominant respiratory pathogen among hospitalized patients with bronchiectasis in Beijing, associated with more extensive structural lung disease, higher systemic inflammation, worse ventilatory function, and prolonged hospitalization. The substantial rates of carbapenem and fluoroquinolone resistance underscore the need for systematic surveillance and antibiotic stewardship in this population.

title: Fourth ventricular cerebral sparganosis mimicking ependymoma with obstructive hydrocephalus: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Cerebral sparganosis is a rare parasitic infection of the central nervous system that usually involves the cerebral parenchyma and may show migratory or tunnel-like imaging features. Direct ventricular involvement is uncommon, and a fourth ventricular mass-forming presentation can closely resemble an intraventricular neoplasm. Case presentation: A 48-year-old man from Yunnan Province, China, presented with more than 5 months of dizziness and headache and two syncopal episodes. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a 2.9 × 2.1 × 3.7 cm rounded lesion centered in the fourth ventricle with focal nodular enhancement and mild supratentorial hydrocephalus. Peripheral eosinophil counts were normal. Ependymoma was considered the leading preoperative diagnosis. Microsurgical resection through a midline suboccipital approach revealed a cystic lesion containing a yellowish nodular cord-like structure. Histopathological examination demonstrated parasitic tegument-like and parenchymal structures with surrounding inflammatory-cell infiltration, consistent with sparganosis. Postoperatively, the patient received praziquantel and supportive therapy. Headache and dizziness resolved, and no recurrence was identified during 5 months of follow-up. Conclusions Fourth ventricular cerebral sparganosis may lack classic parenchymal imaging features and mimic ependymoma. In patients from endemic regions or with relevant exposure, sparganosis should remain in the differential diagnosis of atypical fourth ventricular cystic or nodular enhancing lesions even when peripheral eosinophilia is absent. Intraoperative recognition and histopathological examination can be decisive when preoperative testing is inconclusive.

title: Lightweight Deep Learning for Processing 3D Medical Images: A Systematic Review
abstract: Abstract Deep learning for three dimension (3D) modalities such as CT, MRI, and PET offers promise to improve diagnostic accuracy, surgical planning, and visualization of disease progression, as 3D image data provide high resolution volumetric representation. However, 3D deep learning models are computationally heavy and demand powerful hardware that is not always available or affordable, restrictingtheir use in resource-constrained settings such as rural clinics, edge devices, and low- and middle-income countries. Hence, there is a growing interest in building lightweight deep learning models, in general, and for 3D imaging, in particular. This article systematically and critically reviews lightweight deep learning for processing 3D medical images, examining model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation, quantization, pruning and efficient architectural designs, together with the datasets, tools, and deployment environments involved. These techniques substantially reduce parameters, memory, and inference time with modest accuracy loss. We also identify several research gaps in these approaches, such as the accuracy mismatch between lightweight and standard models, difficulty handling small anatomical structures while keeping models compact, limited testing on real resource-constrained hardware, weak integration of clinical information, and the absence of efficiency-aware evaluation metrics. We outline future directions, cluding robust lightweight designs, purpose-built compact 3D datasets, standardized efficiency metrics, and lightweight multimodal models.

title: Giant Partially Thrombosed Ophthalmic Segment Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm With Severe Angiographic–Radiological Discordance: Implications for Microsurgical Strategy
abstract: Abstract Background Giant partially thrombosed aneurysms of the ophthalmic segment of the internal carotid artery (ICA) present substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because intraluminal thrombus and mural calcification can obscure the true aneurysm morphology, leading to underestimation of lesion size on angiography. Methods A 53-year-old man with progressive headache without focal neurological deficits or objective visual impairment underwent multimodal imaging including CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA. The imaging findings were integrated for operative planning, and microsurgical clipping with staged thrombectomy was performed. Results CT and MRI revealed a giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysm compressing the optic apparatus, whereas DSA depicted only a small residual lumen, demonstrating marked angiographic–radiological discordance. Microsurgical clip reconstruction with staged intraluminal thrombectomy achieved complete aneurysm exclusion with preservation of the parent ICA and ophthalmic artery. The patient recovered without new neurological deficits and remained functionally independent at 6-month follow-up. Conclusions Giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysms may be substantially underestimated by DSA alone. Integration of CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA is critical for defining true aneurysm morphology and optimizing skull base microsurgical strategy. Microsurgical reconstruction with staged thrombectomy remains a definitive treatment option in selected patients.

title: Multimodal Study of Brain Structural Alterations, Functional Gradient Perturbations, and Transcriptomic Specialization in Trigeminal Neuralgia Using 5.0 Tesla MRI
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study aimed to harness the superior imaging capability of 5.0 T MRI to comprehensively characterize structural brain alterations, functional connectome gradient perturbations, and their underlying transcriptomic correlates in patients with trigeminal neuralgia (TN). By constructing an interpretative framework linking macroscopic gradient changes to microscale gene specialization. Methods: Thirty‑five TN patients and sixty‑four healthy controls (HC) were enrolled. All participants underwent 3D high‑resolution T1 and resting‑state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) on a 5.0 T scanner. Functional connectome gradients were derived from the functional connectivity (FC) matrix via diffusion map embedding. Gray matter volume (GMV) was computed using voxel‑based morphometry (VBM), and structure‑function coupling was assessed via spatial correlations. Partial least squares (PLS) regression was employed to identify gene sets associated with gradient perturbations, followed by enrichment analysis to reveal the underlying biological processes. Results: TN patients exhibited attenuated extreme values and increased intermediate values on the primary gradient, with altered gradient scores across multiple networks, indicative of a global gradient compression. GMV reductions was observed in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and superior frontal gyrus (SFG), while gradient scores were decreased in the mPFC and ventral anterior cingulate cortex (vACC). Spatial correlation analyses revealed structure‑function decoupling in the sensorimotor (SMN), limbic (LIB), and frontoparietal (FPN) networks. Transcriptomic analyses showed that cortical gradient perturbations were strongly associated with genes involved in voltage‑gated ion channels, membrane potential regulation, and neurotransmitter release. Significant enrichment of sodium channel, Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase, and GABA receptor genes further corroborated the ion channelopathy basis of TN. Conclusion: 5.0T MRI-based connectome gradient analysis reveals global compression and network-specific reorganization in TN. mPFC/vACC dedifferentiation reflects hierarchical collapse of descending pain inhibition, underpinning chronification. Gene enrichment corroborates ion channelopathy and suggests novel targets. This multi-scale framework integrates structure, function, and transcriptomics to advance mechanistic insights.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Prediction Model for Ureteral Access Sheath Insertion Depth During Flexible Ureteroscopy Based on Patient Anthropometric and Anatomical Parameters
abstract: Abstract Backgound:Optimal placement of UAS during fURS) relies largely on surgeon experience. Insertion that is too deep may cause ureteral injury, whereas insertion that is too shallow necessitates repeated fluoroscopic adjustment. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning model that predicts UAS insertion depth using the L1 vertebra–pubic symphysis distance and readily available anthropometric parameters. Methods This single-center cohort study enrolled 124 consecutive patients who underwent fURS with UAS placement between April 2025 and July 2026. The L1–pubic symphysis distance was measured on preoperative plain radiographs or CT scout images. Candidate predictors included height, age, sex, side, BMI and the L1–pubic symphysis distance. The outcome was the actual UAS insertion depth (cm), measured intraoperatively from the perineal skin to the ureteropelvic junction. The dataset was divided into training (70%, n = 86) and test (30%, n = 38) sets using stratified random sampling by sex. Six regression algorithms were compared, including Ridge regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (Lasso), Bayesian ridge, random forest, support vector regression, and multilayer perceptron. Hyperparameters were tuned by five-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using R², mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and the proportion of predictions within ± 2 cm of the actual depth. The final model was refitted on the entire cohort, and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were obtained for all coefficients. The study followed the Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD) guideline. Results The mean UAS insertion depth was 33.7 ± 2.8 cm (range, 26.5–40.0 cm). Height (r = 0.749), male sex (r = 0.661), L1–pubic symphysis distance (r = 0.563), BMI (r = 0.251), and younger age (r = − 0.498) were correlated with insertion depth. Ridge regression with regularization parameter α = 10 achieved the best balance of accuracy and interpretability, with a test-set R² of 0.661, MAE of 1.24 cm, RMSE of 1.56 cm, and 78.9% of predictions falling within ± 2 cm. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an R² of 0.642 ± 0.067. Leave-one-out cross-validation across all 124 patients produced an R² of 0.649, MAE of 1.39 cm, and 77.4% accuracy within ± 2 cm, substantially outperforming an L1-distance-only model (R² = 0.291; MAE = 1.86 cm). Bootstrap internal validation (1,000 resamples) confirmed minimal overfitting (optimism = 0.026), with an optimism-corrected R² of 0.659, MAE of 1.39 cm, and a calibration slope of 1.033. Standardized coefficients identified male sex (β = 0.927; 95% CI, 0.651–1.205), height (β = 0.811; 95% CI, 0.444–1.148), and L1–pubic symphysis distance (β = 0.740; 95% CI, 0.396–1.086) as the strongest predictors, with BMI also contributing independently (β = 0.410; 95% CI, 0.164–0.674). A freely accessible online calculator was developed for clinical use. Conclusion A multivariable Ridge regression model incorporating the L1–pubic symphysis distance and anthropometric parameters can predict UAS insertion depth with clinically acceptable accuracy. The novel L1–pubic symphysis radiographic measurement, obtainable from routine preoperative imaging without additional examination, contributes independently to depth prediction. External validation in larger and more diverse cohorts is warranted before broad clinical implementation.

title: A Systematic Comparative Literature Review of Biomarkers, Imaging, and Therapeutic Strategies for Endometrial Cancer: Toward an Estrogen Receptor-Guided Near-Infrared Fluorescence Imaging and Endocrine Therapy Pipeline
abstract: Abstract Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynecologic malignancy in high-income countries, with incidence rising alongside increasing obesity and population aging. Diagnosis still depends on invasive tissue biopsy and histopathology, a pathway that is costly, time-consuming, and burdensome for patients. As precision medicine increasingly emphasizes biomarker-guided, minimally invasive strategies, this study systematically compares candidate biomarkers, imaging modalities, and therapeutic strategies to identify the most clinically suitable combination for a minimally invasive diagnostic-therapeutic pipeline for EC. A systematic comparative literature analysis was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and FDA resources, restricted to English-language publications from 2013–2026. Evidence on prevalence, diagnostic accuracy, safety, cost, and therapeutic relevance was organized into weighted decision matrices and a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis. Among five candidate biomarkers, the estrogen receptor (ER) scored highest, reflecting its high prevalence in Type I endometrioid tumors, established assay infrastructure, and direct actionability with endocrine therapy. Among four imaging modalities, near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence endoscopy scored highest based on real-time signal acquisition and compatibility with existing endoscopic infrastructure. Endocrine therapy showed the strongest compatibility with ER-positive disease. Integrating these findings produced a proposed same-day pipeline, ER-targeted NIR fluorescence detection followed by endocrine therapy initiation, with an estimated reduction in time-to-treatment from 10–15 days to under 48 hours. This pipeline offers a scientifically coherent alternative to the conventional biopsy-dependent pathway for Type I, hormone-receptor-positive disease. However, this synthesis is based entirely on published literature; prospective validation, including probe development, imaging accuracy studies, and clinical trials, is required before real-world implementation.

title: MOM-PD: Multimodal Biomarker Optimization for Parkinson's Disease Machine learning-assisted multimodal detection and clinical staging
abstract: Abstract Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) diagnosis relies primarily on clinical motor examination, and the prodromal phase preceding overt motor manifestations remains difficult to identify. No single biomarker modality has been shown to be both sensitive and specific across the full disease spectrum, and how best to integrate multimodal data for stage-specific detection is unclear. Objective: To optimize a multimodal biomarker framework using machine learning based on Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) data, and to define stage-specific biomarkerpanels for manifest PD detection, prodromal identification, and longitudinal progression monitoring. Methods: We analyzed 948 PPMI participants (445 PD, 389 prodromal, 111 healthy controls [HC], 3 SWEDD) with 18 candidate biomarkers spanning dopamine transporter SPECT (DaTscanSBR), structural MRI (FreeSurfer 7 cortical and subcortical metrics), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV. Feature-wide association analysis with Mann-Whitney U tests and Cohen's d was followed by random forest Gini importance ranking. Random forest classifiers (500 trees, 5-fold stratified cross-validation) were trained on three feature sets: (1) DaTscan + clinical; (2) structural MRI only; (3) full multimodal combination. Four-year longitudinal trajectories (BL, V06, V10) of motor scores and grey matter volume were characterized. Results: For PD vs HC, the DaTscan-clinical model achieved near-perfect discrimination (AUC = 0.999, 95% CI 0.997–1.000), far exceeding structural MRI alone (AUC = 0.526). Top discriminative features were putaminal SBR, striatal SBR, and MDS-UPDRS Part III motor score. Prodromal vs HC discrimination was more challenging (AUC = 0.700), with subcortical grey matteratrophy as the leading signal while DaTscan SBR was non-discriminative (P = 0.43). PD vs prodromal classification was excellent (AUC = 0.984). Longitudinally, PD motor scores increased ~1.5 points/year and grey matter volume declined ~0.85%/year. Conclusions: Multimodal biomarkers display staging-dependent complementarity: DaTscan and motor scales dominate manifest PD identification, while subcortical volumetric MRI enablesprodromal detection. Stage-tailored biomarker panels support improved PD phenotyping and early screening for clinical trial enrichment.

title: CAM-Threshold-Guided Weakly Supervised Lesion Segmentation and Relative Lesion-Burden Stratification of Wheat Stripe Rust Using CF2- WRD and Light-UNet
abstract: Abstract Accurate localization and quantification of wheat stripe rust lesions are important for phenotyping and disease management, yet dense pixel-level annotation is costly. We present a Grad-CAM-guided weakly supervised framework that reuses a dual-branch image classifier, CF2-WRD, to generate pseudo-labels for a compact Light-UNet segmenter. The dataset contained 34,694 images in 87 image-level categories, split into 27,834 training, 3,430 validation, and 3,430 test images. CF2-WRD achieved validation and test accuracies of 0.8776 and 0.8711. Among four CAM thresholds, 0.40 produced the highest agreement with CAM-derived validation pseudo-labels (mIoU 0.6584, Dice 0.7101, lesion IoU 0.5555), whereas 0.45 was used as a conservative operating point. Raising the segmentation probability threshold from 0.50 to 0.80 reduced mean predicted lesion-to-leaf ratio from 55.02% to 29.63% in a 300-image subset. The 3,430-image burden distribution was stratified by empirical quartiles. Because no independent manual lesion masks or expert-calibrated severity labels were available, overlap metrics quantify agreement with weak-supervision targets and burden groups represent dataset-relative rankings rather than agronomic severity grades.

title: Culler-Jones Syndrome Across Three Generations: Variable Expressivity of a Pathogenic GLI2 Variant—a Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Culler-Jones syndrome is a rare developmental disorder associated with pathogenic variants in GLI2 gene. The phenotype is highly variable and may include hypopituitarism, growth hormone deficiency, postaxial polydactyly, craniofacial abnormalities, and other developmental abnormalities involving midline structures. Variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance can complicate diagnosis and genetic counseling, particularly when relatives carrying the same pathogenic variant have few or no apparent manifestations. Case presentation A 24-year-old woman of Native American ancestry on both the maternal and paternal sides of her family was referred to the Adult Genetics Clinic for evaluation of congenital craniofacial abnormalities, hypopituitarism, growth hormone deficiency, short stature, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Her history included bilateral cleft lip, anterior cleft palate, midline upper lip and gingival tissue masses, severe growth delay, and abnormal pubertal development. Brain magnetic resonance imaging performed in early childhood demonstrated a Chiari I malformation and absence of most or all of the pituitary gland. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in GLI2 , NM_005270.4:c.1421G>A (p.Trp474*). Targeted familial testing subsequently identified the same variant in her mother, sister, and maternal grandmother, all of whom were reportedly without significant manifestations of GLI2 -related disease. Her brother tested negative for the familial variant. The maternal family history was notable for postaxial polydactyly in multiple relatives. Two maternal uncles reportedly had both postaxial polydactyly and multiple supernumerary nipples, with up to five additional nipples reported in affected individuals. These relatives were not available to undergo genetic testing. Conclusions This family demonstrates marked variable expressivity associated with a pathogenic GLI2 variant across three generations. The proband had a severe multisystem phenotype, whereas three relatives carrying the same variant were reportedly without significant manifestations. Multiple supernumerary nipples in two maternal relatives who have not had molecular confirmation of the GLI2 familial variant represent a potentially new phenotype finding that has not been established as part of the recognized phenotype of Culler-Jones syndrome. This case highlights the importance of detailed family history assessment, cascade testing, and careful genetic counseling in families with GLI2 -related disease.

title: Guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery induced by puncture needle shear injury during cardiac radiofrequency ablation: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Hydrophilic-coated guidewires are essential tools in cardiac interventional procedures. Shear-induced detachment of the hydrophilic coating by a puncture needle represents a rare but potentially serious iatrogenic complication, as dislodged polymer fragments may embolize distally, leading to thrombosis, inflammatory responses, or pulmonary embolism. We present a case of hydrophilic guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery resulting from shear injury by a puncture needle during radiofrequency catheter ablation for a left-sided accessory pathway. Case presentation: A 52-year-old woman with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome underwent radiofrequency catheter ablation. During the procedure, the hydrophilic coating of a guidewire was mechanically stripped by an 18-gauge beveled puncture needle. Fluoroscopy raised suspicion of an intravascular foreign body, and intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) precisely localized two thin, loop-like coating fragments, approximately 6 cm and 3 cm in length, within branches of the right inferior pulmonary artery. The three-dimensional spatial information provided by CBCT directly guided the subsequent percutaneous snare retrieval. Both fragments were successfully retrieved via a minimally invasive percutaneous approach using a goose-neck snare. The patient remained asymptomatic throughout the hospital course, with no procedure-related complications, and was discharged on postoperative day 4. At 3-month follow-up, she continued to be symptom-free. Conclusion Percutaneous snare retrieval is an effective intervention for managing hydrophilic guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery. Increased awareness of this complication, avoidance of withdrawing coated guidewires through metallic needles, routine inspection of device integrity, and intraoperative fluoroscopic monitoring are key preventive strategies.

title: Complete Metabolic Resolution of Residual Low-Grade Oligodendroglioma Following an Apoptosis-Inducing Intervention Initiated Before Radiotherapy: A Case Report with 10-Year Follow-Up
abstract: Abstract Objectives To document a case of residual low-grade oligodendroglioma that showed complete metabolic resolution on ¹⁸F-fluorocholine PET-CT following an independently initiated apoptosis-inducing intervention, with resolution occurring before the commencement of radiotherapy. Methods Longitudinal case report with serial MRI, magnetic resonance spectroscopy, perfusion imaging, and ¹⁸F-fluorocholine PET-CT. The CARE reporting guidelines were followed. Written informed consent was obtained from the patient for anonymized publication. Results A 42-year-old male presented with diplopia and dizziness in November 2015. Imaging revealed a parasagittal low-grade glioma (3.5 × 2.8 × 3 cm), treated with surgical resection. Post-operative MRI documented residual tumor. The patient independently initiated an apoptosis-inducing intervention on approximately April 15, 2016. A transient increase in T2/FLAIR hyperintensity on MRI (May 19, 2016) —interpreted as possible progression— preceded a ¹⁸F-fluorocholine PET-CT on June 3, 2016, which showed no detectable tumor activity. Radiotherapy (20 sessions) commenced in late July 2016 and concluded by August 20, 2016. Metabolic resolution therefore occurred during the period of exclusive exposure to the intervention, before radiotherapy began. Ten years of follow-up have shown complete stability without recurrence. Conclusions This case documents complete metabolic resolution of residual low-grade oligodendroglioma occurring before the initiation of radiotherapy, temporally associated with an apoptosis-inducing intervention. The transient T2 hyperintensity preceding resolution is consistent with a post-apoptotic inflammatory response. These findings warrant formal investigation of the agent's mechanism of action.

title: Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis Risk in Endometrial Cancer Using Multi-Sequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging Combined with Deep Transfer Learning
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and externally validate a nomogram integrating clinical predictors, multisequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics, and deep learning (DL) features for preoperative lymph node metastasis (LNM) prediction in endometrial cancer (EC), and assess the incremental value of DL. Methods: This two-center retrospective study included 520 patients: 268 for training, 117 for held-out internal validation, and 135 for external validation. Radiomics features were extracted from four MRI sequences, and DL features from four ImageNet-pretrained 50-layer residual network (ResNet-50) branches fine-tuned in training. The Clinical+Radiomics model combined four clinical predictors with a radiomics signature; the nomogram additionally incorporated the DL signature. Final models were fitted using all training patients and evaluated unchanged in both validation cohorts. Assessments included DeLong tests, calibration, decision curve analysis, and prespecified sensitivity analysis in magnetic resonance (MR) report-based LNM-negative patients. Results: In internal and external validation, respectively, the nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.866 and 0.886, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of 0.786–0.946 and 0.817–0.955. Corresponding Clinical+Radiomics AUCs were 0.733 (95% CI: 0.591–0.875) and 0.715 (95% CI: 0.594–0.836), favoring the nomogram ( P =0.024 and P <0.001, respectively). Brier scores were 0.110 and 0.083. Decision curves favored the nomogram over comparators at probability thresholds of 0.02–0.39 and 0.01–0.71, respectively. Nomogram AUCs in MR report-based LNM-negative subgroups were 0.843 and 0.858, respectively. Conclusion: Adding DL improved discrimination beyond Clinical+Radiomics. The nomogram may complement preoperative LNM risk stratification but should not replace pathological nodal staging. Prospective multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

Brier scores were 0.110 and 0.083. Decision curves favored the nomogram over comparators at probability thresholds of 0.02–0.39 and 0.01–0.71, respectively. Nomogram AUCs in MR report-based LNM-negative subgroups were 0.843 and 0.858, respectively. Conclusion: Adding DL improved discrimination beyond Clinical+Radiomics. title: Intensity and Landmark Based Registration Under Stain Normalization: A Comparative Study on Differently Stained Histopathology Images
abstract: Abstract Histopathology image registration is crucial for appropriate tissue analysis, especially for the diagnosis of cancer. The presence of staining variation among these whole-slide images leads to several challenges because the stain differs greatly across various tissue types. There are multiple registration techniques, including intensity-based, feature-based, and deep learning-based methods. Although these methods employ different working mechanisms, they all face several challenges, including poor generalization due to staining discrepancies. To address this problem, this study proposed a highly optimized and robust landmark-based registration technique. The technique utilizes anatomical landmarks and employs thin-plate spline interpolation to achieve precise non-rigid alignment, effectively addressing both tissue deformation and staining variability. Moreover, stain normalization was applied using the deep learning-based model StainNet to evaluate how changes in color distribution in images affect the registration approach. Furthermore, the developed approach was comprehensively compared with two well-known intensity-based methods, Elastix and ANTs, under both normalized and raw image conditions. The results from the experiments showed that landmark-based registration was more effective under both conditions in dealing with staining changes than Elastix and ANTs. While Elastix significantly struggled with normalized images due to its reliance on pixel intensities, ANTs showed increased strength after stain normalization; however, they did not perform as well as the method based on landmarks. Although, landmark-based registration is reliable as it is not influenced by varying staining but it is still challenging to annotate the landmarks with significant accuracy that can be improved in future techniques by using automated landmark annotations.

title: Molecular landscape of medullary nephrocalcinosis in children – a nationwide, prospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to investigate the genetic landscape and to identify predictors of a molecular diagnosis in pediatric nephrocalcinosis. Methods This prospective, nationwide cohort study enrolled 79 unrelated pediatric patients with ultrasound-based medullary nephrocalcinosis of unknown etiology. Genetic evaluation was conducted using whole-exome sequencing ( n = 75) or targeted (Sanger) sequencing ( n = 4). Only (likely)pathogenic variants were considered diagnostic. Results A molecular diagnosis of Mendelian disease (MD) was established in 16% of patients, which included infantile hypercalcemia type 1 ( CYP24A1 , n = 3) and type 2 ( SLC34A1 , n = 2), familial hypomagnesemia, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis ( CLDN16 , n = 2; CLDN19 , n = 1), distal renal tubular acidosis ( ATP6V0A4 , n = 1; ATP6V1B1 , n = 1), Bartter syndrome type 2 ( KCNJ1 , n = 1) and type 3 ( CLCNKB , n = 1), and Dent disease type 1 ( CLCN5 , n = 1). Monoallelic (MA) variants, possibly predisposing to nephrocalcinosis, were found in 16% of patients, encompassing four genes, predominantly within the SLC34A1 and SLC34A3 (61%). In patients with MD, except for two patients with Bartter syndrome, typical phenotypes were observed, in contrast to carriers of MA variants, in whom the majority had subtle abnormalities. Clinical parameters, prematurity and family history for nephrocalcinosis/lithiasis were not associated with MD diagnoses. Conclusions This study clarifies the distinct genetic architecture of pediatric nephrocalcinosis. The data may possibly explain the etiology in approximately 30% of cases, when considering both MD and MA variants. Disease-specific phenotypes are associated with MD; however, the absence of typical features should not preclude a genetic diagnosis.

title: The Changing Burden of Multiple Sclerosis in Bahrain, 2013–2026: Foundational Epidemiology, Contemporary Registry-Based Case Ascertainment, and Genetic Insights in a Changing Arabian Gulf MS Landscape
abstract: Abstract Background Bahrain’s 2011–2013 multiple sclerosis (MS) registry established the country’s first epidemiological baseline using the 2010 McDonald criteria. Since then, diagnostic criteria, MRI access, specialist care, and follow-up have evolved, while Bahrain and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) studies suggest HLA and non-HLA susceptibility signals. The present analysis links the foundational baseline to March 2026 registry-based case ascertainment and a one-year new-diagnosis count, allowing contemporary prevalence and incidence to be considered together while preserving the distinction between registry ascertainment and a formal population survey. Objective To compare the 2013 and 2026 clinically recognized MS burden among Bahraini citizens, quantify contemporary crude registry-based prevalence and incidence, and contextualize the findings with emerging Bahraini and GCC genetic and environmental evidence. Materials and Methods This retrospective registry-based descriptive analysis included 287 Bahraini patients fulfilling the 2010 McDonald criteria and identified through Salmaniya Medical Complex between 1 July 2011 and 31 October 2013. The March 2026 count combined Salmaniya Medical Complex and National Bank of Bahrain Multiple Sclerosis Centre records. Crude prevalence was estimated from 876 actively followed patients using a Bahraini-citizen denominator of 747,500, with sensitivity analysis across 745,000–755,000. From March 2025 to March 2026, 48 newly diagnosed Bahraini patients were registered; crude registry-based incidence and an exact Poisson 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated. Only aggregate data were analyzed. Contemporary GCC epidemiology and relevant diagnostic, environmental, genetic, and treatment evidence were reviewed narratively. Results The foundational cohort had a female-to-male ratio of 2.49:1, mean age at onset of 35 ± 10.2 years, median Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 2.0, reported prevalence of 59.9 per 100,000 Bahraini citizens (recalculated 95% CI, 53.0–66.8), and annual incidence of 5.8 per 100,000 (95% CI, 2.8–8.87) during 2012–2013. By March 2026, 876 patients were actively followed, 589 more than the foundational count and 3.05-fold that count. Estimated crude registry-based prevalence was 117.2 per 100,000 (95% CI, 109.4–125.0; sensitivity range, 116.0–117.6). The 48 newly diagnosed patients yielded a crude registry-based incidence of 6.4 per 100,000 (95% CI, 4.7–8.5). Conclusion Bahrain’s clinically recognized MS burden has increased substantially, while the contemporary one-year incidence estimate remains broadly similar to the earlier estimate. This pattern is compatible with a combination of epidemiological change, cumulative prevalence, improved ascertainment, diagnostic sensitivity, survival, and specialist follow-up rather than a proportional rise in annual new diagnoses. Differences in diagnostic eras and ascertainment preclude direct causal attribution. Prospective national registration integrating clinical, imaging, treatment, environmental, and genetic data is needed to define the evolving burden and its determinants.

title: Distance mapping analysis of tibiotalar joint in varus ankle osteoarthritis using 3D bone reconstruction of weight-bearing CT scans
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Varus ankle osteoarthritis (OA) is a common condition in which malalignment-related eccentric loading leads to progressive medial joint degeneration. Surgical treatment decision depends on the extent and distribution of joint space narrowing. Weight-bearing computed tomography (WBCT) combined with three-dimensional (3D) bone reconstruction software now enables distance mapping analysis, which can quantify regional tibiotalar joint space more precisely than conventional radiography. The purpose of this study was to visualize and quantify regional joint space narrowing patterns of the tibiotalar joint across stages of varus ankle OA using an auto-segmentation technique and distance mapping analysis applied to WBCT images. Methods In this retrospective study, WBCT scans of 60 ankles from 36 patients were obtained and classified according to the modified Takakura classification into three groups: control (stage 0–1; n = 29), moderate OA (stages 2 and 3a; n = 19), grouped based on joint space narrowing confined to the medial gutter, and severe OA (stages 3b and 4; n = 12), defined by obliteration extending to the talar dome. All WBCT images were analyzed using 3D auto-segmentation and distance mapping software (Bonelogic® Ortho Foot and Ankle, Disior, Finland). The talar articular surface was divided into eight regions of interest (two medial gutter and six talar dome sub-regions), and the joint space distance was measured as the shortest surface-to-surface distance from each point on the talus to the adjacent tibial plafond. Results Compared with controls, the moderate OA group showed significantly reduced distances at the anterior medial gutter (MMA: 2.14 ± 0.06 vs. 1.76 ± 0.11 mm, p = 0.033), the anteromedial talar dome (TMA: 2.71 ± 0.10 vs. 2.35 ± 0.11 mm, p < 0.001), and the central posterior dome (TCP: 2.54 ± 0.06 vs. 2.42 ± 0.14 mm, p < 0.001). In the severe OA group, further reductions were observed across medial and central dome regions, with the most pronounced narrowing at the anteromedial dome (TMA: 1.34 ± 0.15 mm, p < 0.001 vs. controls), and significant decreases at the posteromedial dome, and both anterior and posterior central dome (all p < 0.01 vs. controls). No significant changes were detected at the lateral talar dome (TLA, TLP) across any group comparison. Conclusion WBCT-based distance mapping revealed that joint space narrowing in varus ankle OA follows a characteristic spatial pattern: moderate disease predominantly affects the anterior medial gutter and anteromedial dome, while severe disease extends across medial and central dome regions with consistent lateral preservation. These findings provide 3D quantitative support for the clinical importance of talar dome involvement in severity grading. In preoperative planning for realignment osteotomy, distance mapping may help identify the regions of degenerative cartilage loss and guide load redistribution toward preserved areas, particularly the lateral talar dome and posterior medial gutter.

title: Chronic Cerebral Small Vessel Disease Burden and Acute Infarction in Relation to Functional Brain Network Efficiency: A Cross-Sectional Resting-State fMRI Study
abstract: Abstract Background Chronic cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) and acute infarction frequently coexist, but their respective relationships with functional network integration remain uncertain. We examined whether cumulative CSVD burden and clinical acute infarction were independently associated with resting-state functional global efficiency and explored which lesion phenotypes and anatomical regions showed the strongest associations. Methods This hospital-based cross-sectional study included 166 patients aged 45 years or older with suspected cerebrovascular disease. Automated multisequence MRI segmentation quantified white matter hyperintensities, recent small subcortical infarcts, lacunes, perivascular spaces, and cerebral microbleeds. Resting-state functional networks were constructed using a 90-region anatomical parcellation, with global efficiency prespecified as the primary outcome. HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, mean framewise displacement, and clinical acute infarction. Regional markers were jointly evaluated within each lesion family, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Results Higher total CSVD burden was independently associated with lower global efficiency (B per 1-point increase = − 0.0055, 95% CI: −0.0086 − 0.0024; P < 0.001), whereas clinical acute infarction was not (B = 0.0008, 95% CI: −0.0071–0.0087; P = 0.850). The lacune regional block explained an additional 9.27% of variance (robust P = 0.00195). Parietal lacunes (B=-0.0130, FDR q = 0.026) and deep lacunes (B=-0.0132, FDR q = 0.021) were independently associated with lower global efficiency. Regional cerebral microbleed, perivascular-space, and white-matter-hyperintensity blocks were not statistically significant. Conclusions Greater cumulative CSVD burden, particularly parietal and deep lacunes, was associated with impaired functional network integration, whereas clinical acute infarction showed no independent association in this cohort. These cross-sectional findings identify anatomically informative correlates but do not establish causal or temporal relationships.

title: Histopathological Profile of Tobacco-Associated Oral Mucosal Lesions in Chronic Cigarette Smokers: A Five-Year Retrospective Study from a Tertiary Care Centre in Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Background Tobacco smoking has been recognised as one of the key risk factors associated with a wide spectrum of oral mucosal alterations, ranging from benign reactive changes and epithelial dysplasia to malignant oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Hence, in a population with high tobacco exposure, histopathological assessment remains central to characterise and diagnose potentially malignant and malignant disorders. Objective To evaluate the histopathological profile of tobacco-induced oral mucosal lesions among chronic cigarette smokers and to determine the incidence and degree of epithelial dysplasia and other smoking-associated histological alterations. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional study was carried out in the Department of Histopathology, Ziauddin University Hospital, Karachi, Pakistan. Histopathologically verified oral mucosal biopsy specimens obtained from chronic cigarette smokers from January 2020 to January 2026 were analysed. Information regarding demographics, smoking status, and clinical and histopathological data was derived from archived records. Hematoxylin and eosin-stained microscopic sections were used to study epithelial and stromal changes; epithelial dysplasia was classified according to World Health Organisation criteria. SPSS version 26.0 was used to analyse the data. Results The study was based on 50 oral mucosal biopsy specimens. The study population showed male dominance, with a mean age of 51.79 ± 13.39 years. Buccal mucosa was the most commonly affected anatomical site, while moderately differentiated infiltrative OSCC was the prominent histopathological diagnosis detected in 12 cases (24%). 50% of dysplastic lesions were mild, whereas moderate and severe lesions each accounted for 25%. Conclusion Chronic smoking was linked with a broad range of histopathological alterations in the oral mucosa. A substantial number of cases showed epithelial dysplasia and invasive OSCC. For those with long term use of tobacco, early detection and timely biopsy with histopathological analysis are crucial to identify potential malignant lesions and assess their development. Study findings may help optimise screening and preventive strategies for tobacco-attributed oral cancer in susceptible populations.

title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Model Integrating Multiparametric MRI Features and PSA for Differentiating Benign and Malignant Prostate Nodules
abstract: Abstract Objective: To develop a multimodal diagnostic model integrating radiomics features, deep learning features derived from prostate multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels, and to investigate its value in differentiating benign and malignant prostate nodules, thereby providing an auxiliary tool for the noninvasive diagnosis of prostate cancer and clinical decision-making. Methods: A total of 312 patients with prostate nodules confirmed by pathology were retrospectively enrolled and randomly divided into training and test sets at an 8:2 ratio. Radiomics and deep learning features were extracted from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, and were combined with PSA levels to construct multimodal diagnostic models. Five models were developed, including the ADC model, DWI model, T2WI model, mpMRI model, and mpMRI_PSA model. Five-fold cross-validation was used for model training. Model performance was evaluated in the test set using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1 score. The DeLong test was used to compare the differences in AUC between the best-performing model and the other models. A P value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: All five models demonstrated a certain ability to differentiate benign from malignant prostate nodules. The AUCs of the ADC, DWI, T2WI, mpMRI, and mpMRI_PSA models were 0.73, 0.79, 0.84, 0.94, and 0.97, respectively. The diagnostic performance progressively improved with the integration of multiple MRI sequences compared with individual sequences. Further incorporation of PSA resulted in the best diagnostic performance for the mpMRI_PSA model, which outperformed the other models in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. The DeLong test demonstrated that the differences in AUC between the best-performing mpMRI_PSA model and the ADC, DWI, T2WI, and mpMRI models were all statistically significant ( P < 0.05). Conclusion: The multimodal diagnostic model integrating radiomics and deep learning features from prostate mpMRI with PSA levels demonstrated high discriminative performance for differentiating benign and malignant prostate nodules. Its diagnostic performance was superior to that of the single-sequence models and the mpMRI-only model, suggesting that it may serve as a potential auxiliary tool for the noninvasive differential diagnosis of prostate cancer and clinical decision-making.

title: Comparative Prognostic Value of 11 C-Methionine and 18 F-FDG PET/CT for Tumor Progression and Hearing Deterioration in NF2-Related Vestibular Schwannomas
abstract: Abstract Purpose. To compare the metabolic imaging characteristics and prognostic value of 11 C-methionine and 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT in NF2-related vestibular schwannomas. Methods. This single-center retrospective cohort included 22 adults with 40 untreated vestibular schwannomas who underwent baseline 11 C-MET and 18 F-FDG PET/CT and audiological assessment. Median follow-up was 21 months. Tracer uptake and tumor-to-cerebellum ratios were compared. Receiver operating characteristic and Cox regression analyses evaluated associations with volumetric tumor progression and hearing deterioration. Results. Although maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) was higher with 18 F-FDG than with 11 C-MET (3.69 ± 1.12 vs 3.08 ± 0.83; P < .001), maximum tumor-to-background ratio (TBRmax) was substantially higher with 11 C-MET (2.43 ± 0.59 vs 0.54 ± 0.14; P < .0001). For predicting tumor progression, 11 C-MET TBRmax achieved an area under the curve of 0.753, compared with 0.507 for 18 F-FDG TBRmax (P = .02). Corresponding values for hearing deterioration were 0.736 and 0.531. In multivariable analysis, 11 C-MET TBRmax independently predicted tumor progression (hazard ratio, 2.958; 95% confidence interval, 1.380–6.339; P = .0053) and hearing deterioration (hazard ratio, 3.223; 95% confidence interval, 1.021–10.172; P = .046). No 18 F-FDG-derived parameter was significantly associated with either outcome. Conclusion. 11 C-MET PET/CT provided superior tumor-to-background contrast and stronger prognostic information than 18 F-FDG PET/CT in NF2-related vestibular schwannomas. These findings support prospective evaluation of 11 C-MET TBRmax as an imaging biomarker for individualized surveillance.

title: 18F-FET-PET/MRI versus Standard MRI for Radiotherapy Planning in High-Grade Brain Glioma: A Pilot Study (FETSMaRT)
abstract: Abstract Purpose High-grade gliomas carry a poor prognosis, and MRI-based radiotherapy (RT) planning may inadequately capture metabolically active tumor infiltration. ¹⁸F-fluoroethyl-tyrosine (FET) PET provides superior tumor delineation, yet prospective North American evidence supporting integration with RT planning remains limited. Methods FETSMaRT enrolled 30 patients with WHO grade 3 or 4 high-grade glioma receiving post-operative RT. FET-PET/MRI was acquired before RT with the radiation oncologist blinded to PET, enabling retrospective quantification of discordance between MRI-based and FET-PET/MRI-derived gross tumor (GTV), clinical target (CTV), and planning target (PTV) volumes. In the glioblastoma subgroup (n = 23), Kaplan–Meier and Cox analyses related GTV and CTV discordance to time to progression. Results Median age was 60 years; 77% had glioblastoma and 60% MGMT promoter methylation. GTV discordance occurred in 17/30 patients (56.7%) and CTV discordance in 15/30 (50.0%). FET-PET/MRI-derived volumes significantly exceeded MRI-based volumes for GTV (43.6 vs 38.6 cc; p < 0.0001), CTV (119.2 vs 110.8 cc; p = 0.0045), and PTV (171.1 vs 159.6 cc; p = 0.0003). Larger GTV∆ and CTV∆ change values were associated with numerically shorter median time to progression, but neither association was statistically significant. Radiation treatment failures were predominantly central (60.0%). Conclusion FET-PET/MRI-derived target volumes were significantly larger than MRI-based volumes, confirming systematic underestimation of metabolically active tumor extent by anatomical MRI. While not meeting significance in this pilot study, directional CTV and GTV discordance suggests a possible association with progression; these exploratory pilot data nonetheless justify a prospective trial of FET-PET-guided RT in high-grade glioma. NCT06499831

title: Canadian Preterm Brain Injury Consensus Classification for Cranial Ultrasound and Prediction of Neurodevelopmental Outcome in Preterm Infants
abstract: Abstract Objective To determine whether classification of severe preterm brain injury using the Canadian cranial ultrasound (cUS) consensus improves prediction of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Study Design Infants born < 29 weeks’ gestation (2010–2018) with ≥ 3 cUS examinations, any brain injury, and neurodevelopmental assessment at 18–24 months were studied. Brain injury was assessed from serial cUS using the Canadian consensus classification. Severe injury comprised high-grade intraventricular hemorrhage, severe post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation, cystic white matter injury, and/or moderate-large cerebellar hemorrhage. Associations with death and/or significant neurodevelopmental impairment were analyzed and compared with historical reporting. Results Among 231 infants, 45% had severe brain injury and 39% experienced adverse outcome. Severe injury was independently associated with adverse outcome (OR 5.44, 95% CI 2.85–10.74). Sensitivity was similar to historical reporting, but specificity for cerebral palsy and severe cognitive delay was higher. Conclusions The Canadian cUS consensus classification improves neurodevelopmental outcome prediction and may inform early intervention and neuroprotective strategies.
